articleTitle: Custom Design of CXL Controller on Intel FPGA R-Tile
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: To meet the high bandwidth and low latency communication requirements between modern computer processors and accelerators or memories, for applications such as in data center processing, and "multi-GPU and CPU" in machine learning (ML), in the latter case though NVLink (2014) and the latest UALink (2024) are available, while CXL (Compute Express Link) has been developed in 2019 and continuously provides a cache consistent interconnect technology between CPU and device, as well as between devices. This article reports the custom design of CXL controller on Intel FPGA R-Tile architecture. The R-Tile supports PHY Interface for PCI Express (PIPE) direct mode, it can provide up to 16 SerDes (serializer / deserializer) channels. The PIPE SerDes mode interface is connected to the custom controller implemented in soft IP through the Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB). The CXL custom controller designed includes the Logic Physical Layer (PHY) and Medium Access Control (MAC), Data Link Layer (DLL) and Transaction Layer (TL), that includes the Transmitter (TX) and Receiver (RX). The custom controller design of this CXL device is expected to promote efficient data transmission, expand memory bandwidth and capacity, efficiently meet complex computing requirements, and significantly improve system performance, further verification and application are to be applied.

articleTitle: A Study on Correlation Between WAT and CP Yields Based on Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Wafer Acceptance Testing (WAT) parameters reflect Chip Probing (CP) yields, prompting extensive discussions on their correlation. This paper proposes an effective process to explore this relationship. Based on theoretical analysis, a classifier is developed to accurately identify CP yields reflected by WAT, with precision exceeding 95%. In the model training phase, deep learning methods are used to address challenges like data imbalance and missing labels, reducing prediction errors by 71% compared to the baseline. Experiments show that this process provides more accurate and interpretable insights into the WAT-CP yield relationship for mass-produced ICs.

articleTitle: Fault Sensitivity Enhancement for Rram-Based Neuromorphic Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The complexity of resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based neuromorphic computing systems (RNCS) and the variety of faults make on-line testing challenging. We propose an Iterative Fast Gradient Sign Method (IFGSM) for enhancing the fault sensitivity of RNCS tests. This is accomplished by exploiting the sensitivity of neural networks to weight perturbations. This method is able to enhance the sensitivity to fault perturbations using tests applied only to the primary I/O. Statistical analysis shows that the tests based on IFGSM are more sensitive to small changes in the RNCS than standard test approach.

articleTitle: A General Auto Configured Characterization Test Program Generation Solution on Advantest V93000 ATE Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Characterization (char) Test Program verifies the minimum power supply voltage, leakage current, and analog characteristics required by each corner chip at different operating frequencies and temperatures to combine the client's application conditions and ultimately define the ATE test conditions. A characterization auto generation solution is proposed at advantest V93000 platform and users only need to define file path information and describe char test plan as required.

articleTitle: Time-dependence Dielectric Breakdown of Novel Dopant-Segregated Tunneling Field Effect Transistors Based on Foundry Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, the time-dependence dielectric breakdown (TDDB) of the novel dopant-segregated tunneling field effect transistor (DS-TFET) based on the standard CMOS baseline platform is investigated and compared with conventional MOSFET. Results show that the TDDB lifetime under operation voltage exceeds 10 years, while the maximum overdrive voltage of DS-TFET is lower than MOSFET, indicating the importance of reliability-aware design for low voltage applications.

articleTitle: Ferroelectric Materials, Devices and Chip Technologies for Enhanced Computational and Storage Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The paper discussed recent progresses of hafnium oxide-based ferroelectric materials, devices and chip technologies which improves the performance, reliability and energy efficiency, indicating the feasibility of ferroelectric devices for computational and storage enhancement.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of DED Process in Embedded Semi-Floating Gate
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The embedded semi-floating gate (SFG) structure is characterized by its gate with charge storage capability. However, during the embedded processes for array integration, this structure can lead to challenges such as high aspect ratio of poly trench etching and the formation of poly voids during poly filling. Additionally, it will produce step height which cause surface damage to logic circuits during poly chemical mechanical polishing (CMP). To address these issues, this paper proposed the use of a DED (deposition-etch-deposition) method. By reducing the trench aspect ratio and optimizing poly deposition, combined with a skip poly CMP process integration, we have achieved void-free poly deposition while minimizing poly pattern loading, thereby effectively protecting the logic circuits.

articleTitle: Timing Sequence Optimization Methods For Cross-Die Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: 2.5D/3D SIC technologies are developing rapidly nowadays due to its many benefits. To optimize the data timing across dies, two methods are introduced including reserving setup/hold margins through using timing-margin optimization modules across die-interface and also including applying customized buffers with strong driving capabilities to reduce delay, so as to solve the timing problems of cross-die data transmission, increasing the test frequency and thus optimize the test cost of multi-die chips.

articleTitle: A Novel Solution to Improve Reliability Characteristics of Advanced Node ETOX NOR-flash Memory
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A novel solution to improve the top corner rounding of shallow trench isolation (STI) and time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) characteristics of peripheral circuit has been investigated in 4X-nm serial peripheral interface (SPI) NOR-flash memory cells with self-aligned STI architecture. The cell active area (CAA) last approach of integrated manufacturing process is implemented, where the CAA loop is formed after the completion of peripheral active area (PAA) loop, thereinto, the integrated PAA loop includes the process of peripheral STI trench etching, peripheral STI gap-filling, densification and planarization. Good peripheral STI top corner rounding and reliability results of peripheral MOSFET are obtained by process optimization of PAA loop. In this paper, the novel structure with CAA-last manufacturing process is provided to give insight into the improvement of reliability characteristics upon the shrunken cell geometry of advanced node NOR-flash technology featuring a self-aligned source ETOX architecture.

articleTitle: Electrical Characteristics of IGZO Thin Film Transistors Fabricated by Magnetron Sputtering with Controlled Mean Free Path of Sputtered Particles
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study investigates the optimization of indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) thin film transistors (TFT) by refining magnetron sputtering parameters and applying post-deposition annealing. Controlling argon-to-oxygen ratios and gas flow influenced the mean free path, enhancing film density and electronic properties. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed that while higher oxygen ratios during deposition improved metal-oxygen bonding, post-deposition annealing was critical in minimizing defects and enhancing film stability. The optimized IGZO TFTs demonstrated a stable threshold voltage, a subthreshold swing of 100 mV/dec, and a hysteresis of 42 mV, advancing low-power oxide TFT technology.

articleTitle: Silicon-Rich ONO Thickness Prediction Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Oxide-Nitride-Oxide (ONO) structure is essential in SONOS memory devices, as it enables charge trapping and release to store information. This study introduces an innovative composite sandwich structure composed of silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">₂</inf>), silicon nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">₃</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">₄</inf>), silicon-rich nitride (SiNx), and nitride-oxide layers. The research investigates how deposition parameters such as temperature, time, and other variables influence the thickness of the film, which directly impacts device performance and reliability. To optimize and predict film thickness accurately, the study employs the ResNet18 deep learning model. This model provides precise control over the deposition process, ensuring enhanced consistency and reliability of SONOS devices.

articleTitle: Simulation-Driven Optimization of STI Etching: A Systematic Approach to Defect Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The shallow trench isolation (STI) etching process frequently faces defects like etch stop and pitting, resulting from complex interactions across multiple steps. In this study, calibrated simulations were pivotal in systematically analyzing these defects. The simulations allowed us to predict how variations in process parameters, particularly oxygen concentration, contributed to the etch stop, enabling us to optimize the gas ratio and achieve uniform etching rapidly. Additionally, simulations guided the introduction of a breakthrough step and the adjustment of the stripe process sequence, leading to significant reductions in pitting. This simulation-driven approach, validated by experimental results, proved highly efficient in identifying the root causes of these defects and determining the optimal process recipe for STI etching.

articleTitle: Through-Pitch CD Control with TiN metal hardmask etch Process in Logic BEOL Patterning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The large amounts of through-pitch critical dimension (CD) data are required for generating the optical proximity effect (OPE) curves, which are the most sensitive ones to lithography scanner illumination setting and the following patterning transfer plasma etch process in semiconductor manufacturing. Etching process of TiN metal hardmask (MHM) with ArF photo resist (PR) are applied for this experiment. The test reticle contains line/space patterns in a range of pitch between 114nm and 900nm, and the target CD is 52nm for the dense line. The results of this study demonstrate that iso-dense loading of AEI (after etching inspection) is tunable from +16.1nm to -2.5nm by etch process tuning knobs, such as pressure, bias RF voltage, CF4 and additional N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas, during MHM patterning.

articleTitle: Use IOT Technology to Optimize ATE Test Cell Operations and Management
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Historically, point solutions were widely used for ATE test cell operation such as production test, maintenance, status monitoring, data collection and analysis. This creates numerous test cell integration challenges.As a key enabler of Industry 4.0, IoT is a convergence of embedded systems, network connectivity, real time monitoring and remote control, and automation. This paper proposes building solutions upon IoT which provides a common architectural ground for test cell operations and management. Better consistency, compatibility, interoperability, and scalability can be achieved.

articleTitle: Enhanced Floating Random Walk Algorithm for Capacitance Extraction Considering Damage Effects
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced Floating Random Walk (FRW) algorithm designed to address the challenges in 3D capacitance extraction caused by damage effects in semiconductor manufacturing processes. These damage effects, arising from process-induced stress and material deformation, lead to non-Manhattan geometries and variations in dielectric properties, which complicate traditional extraction methods. The improved FRW algorithm incorporates adaptive techniques such as a rotating transition cube and a spherical Gaussian surface to accurately model the irregular geometries and dielectric inhomogeneities. This approach improves the accuracy and efficiency of capacitance extraction, effectively accounting for the geometric distortions and material changes introduced by damage effects in advanced integrated circuits.

articleTitle: A Streamlined Electro-Thermal-Mechanical Simulation Method for Power Semiconductor Packaging Design
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates an efficient electro-thermal -mechanical simulation process for validating MOSFET packaging designs. Two PCB copper layouts and two packaging designs are discussed regarding to weak or risk points in current density and temperature distributions. Methods for validating solder joint electromigration and stress under power cycling are proposed. The study offers a streamlined simulation framework for packaging design of power semiconductor devices at operational currents.

articleTitle: The Impact of Pid on The Degradation of LDMOS
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Plasma-induced damage (PID) during semiconductor fabrication processes, such as inter-layer dielectric (ILD) and inter-metal dielectric (IMD) deposition and metal etching, poses significant challenges to device reliability. Generally, when gate oxide (GOX) thickness is above direct tunneling limit, PID is expected to decrease as the GOX thickness increases. Contrary to the conventional understanding, this work reveals that PID also contributes to the degradation of LDMOS devices with GOX thicknesses exceeding 10 nm, especially with field plate structure. It leads to the proposal of a novel hypothesis involving charge accumulation in or around the field plate. This work provides a novel perspective on the reliability of LDMOS and offers strategies to mitigate its adverse effects on LDMOS.

articleTitle: An Approach to Improve Distortion with High-Aspect-Ratio Cryogenic Etching Using BORON-Containing Gases
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Cryogenic etching is building a "high-speed railway" in high-aspect-ratio (HAR) channel hole patterning due to its enhanced etch rates and improved profile. However, shape-deformation or circularity distortion of holes appears with increased aspect ratio. Here, we report a novel process associated with boron-containing gas, such as BCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> or BF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, provide a positive effect on maintaining hole circularity from top to bottom. By tuning addition mode and amount of B-based gas, the hole distortion can be significantly improved even if the temperature is as low as -60C. The findings can provide guidance for process optimization in very high-aspect-ratio etch to meet advanced memory devices.

articleTitle: The SAS Implant Integration Optimization in the Cell Scaling of 4Xnm ETOX NOR Flash
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Vertical direction polysilicon height down plays an important role in the cell size shrink of ETOX NOR flash, and the Self-aligned source (SAS) implant process is one of the restrict factor of polysilicon height. In this paper, we optimize the SAS loop implant process energy and dosage to achieve an ingenious balance between source side implant ion and the punch through of tunneling oxide. Finally, the performance of optimized of SAS loop process are investigated by the wafer accept test (WAT), chip probe (CP) and TCAD simulation.

articleTitle: Effects of ALE Capabilities and DC Pulsing in Microwave ECR Plasma on Etching Processes for Cutting-Edge Logic LSI
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper discusses the application of a microwave ECR plasma etching system, which has diverse pulsing functions and ALE (Atomic Layer Etching) capabilities for logic LSI. In fin and WFM/HK etching, verticality and planarity were achieved by applying ALE capabilities pulsing at low gas pressure. In WFM patterning, WFM erosion at the fin top was minimized while eliminating nm-level space residues. We successfully improved this trade-off by employing a novel technology called DC pulsing, which mitigates the charge-up effect.

articleTitle: Investigation of silicon oxide thin film utilizing plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition in ICP etcher
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) has become critical in semiconductor manufacturing because the film thickness and uniformity are controllable at the atomic scale. Silicon oxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) thin films are deposited by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) using a Si precursor and oxygen plasmas at room temperature. The deposition process is conducted in an inductively coupled plasma(ICP) chamber and the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films are formed at several angstroms per cycle. In addition, the ALD coverage profile on different patterns and the parameters that affect the coverage profile of sidewall protective film in HAR patterns are investigated.

articleTitle: Pad Physical Properties Effects on Removal Rate in a STI Ceria CMP Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As one of the main consumables of chemical mechanical polishing, pad plays an important role in providing mechanical polishing force, carrying and distributing polishing fluid and removing polishing by-products during chemical mechanical grinding. In recent years, with the progress of chip process nodes, CMP technology has become more and more important, and has become an indispensable flattening process for processes below 0.35um, and the requirements for CMP consumables are also increasing. It is well known that abrasive pads are closely related to wafer defect and uniformity. In this article, we introduce an excellent abrasive Pad with polishing pads, cushioning layers, additives, and microspheres. This includes adjusting the pore distribution of Top Pad and uniformity with the unique hole design of sub Pad. Developed both flexible and rigid pad, combined with the particle size, charge, component characteristics of slurry the size of grinding disc by drilling arrangement, the change of Remove Rate during the whole lifetime is less than 100A/s, and the sensitivity of 300mm wafer edge thickness to pressure can reach ±20% response. Easier to adjust Profile and with the help of functional software such as LUT/iAPC/FVXE, Uniformity remains high. Aiming at defect, this abrasive pad also adjusts the ratio of soft and hard chains/the number of microspheres, so that the inline Wafer Suffer Micro Scratch is basically maintained at about 2 per piece.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Multiplexer Solution for IC Testing on the V93000
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of the electronics industry, chip’s function has been becoming more complex and powerful, as well as the higher integration of device. In this paper, we have introduced a low-cost multiplexer (MUX) solution for IC test on V93000 testing platform<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. On the hardware side, we propose MUX on load board (LB) design to optimize Automated Test Equipment (ATE) channel utilization. On the software side, we developed a MUX framework which leveraging Java8’s new features, using lambda expressions to realize function interface, making the program more concise, flexible, and easy to maintain, significantly reducing the overall testing cost.

articleTitle: Addressing Missing Die Data in CD-SEM Analysis: A Direction-Weighted KNN Approch
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, handling missing values in measurement data is a crucial step to ensure accurate data analysis or feature extraction. Traditional interpolation algorithms, such as K-nearest neighbor (KNN), have been widely used to estimate missing die locations on wafer maps. However, when applied to CD-SEM measured wafer maps in lithography, such interpolation methods may not accurately approximate the true data due to the lack of consideration for lithography process characteristics. This paper proposes a modified direction-weighted KNN interpolation algorithm with considerations of scanner exposure direction. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the modified algorithm more effectively represents the feature data after interpolation, leading to better alignment with the original wafer map.

articleTitle: Contact Silicon Etch Challenge in IGBT Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Contact is an important process in semiconductor fabrication. This paper aims at Contact Etch Process in IGBT manufacturing, which will etch both contact VIA and contact trench at one etch stage. We overcame challenges of Bottom morphology, Side-wall profile, Recess depth loading and WIW etch uniformity, those are required in IGBT contact etch process. The process was developed in NAURA NMC612C® etch system.

articleTitle: An Integrated Solution for Optimizing the Idsat Performance of 55 nm BCD Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The 55 nm BCD(Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) technology has become a critical platform for advanced mixed-signal and power ICs (integrated circuits), making the improvement of its electrical performance essential for further development. This article proposes an optimization involves adjusting the amount and sequence of gate oxide wet etching to address the issue of gate oxide over-etching and replacing the single-layer oxide structure with an ONO (Oxide-Nitride-Oxide)-based SAB (Salicide Block) structure to mitigate spacer damage caused by intensive wet processes. Both measures significantly contribute to reducing I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> and their combined application demonstrates a stronger synergistic effect. This integrated approach offers a practical and effective solution for optimizing the electrical characteristics of 55 nm BCD devices.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Hotspots EPE Propagation Through Step-By-Step SEM Contour Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In high-volume manufacturing (HVM), accurately identifying process issues is essential, as it directly influences both product quality and production efficiency. Effective fault localization allows teams to quickly detect and address potential defects, thereby minimizing resource waste and delays. However, troubleshooting process problems often involves indirect data analysis. Teams must monitor and analyze changes in various parameters, including recipe settings, environmental conditions, and equipment performance, to infer the underlying root causes.This article presents a novel troubleshooting approach based on contour and statistical analysis. By directly comparing graphical differences between process steps and analyzing changes in critical dimension (CD) distribution, this method identifies issues from overall process variations down to specific changes caused by individual steps. This approach not only streamlines troubleshooting but also significantly reduces the time required to resolve problems.Moreover, the method goes beyond simple variation detection by quantifying differences using CD values. It disaggregates localized variations within SEM image dimensions, providing detailed insights into the extent of deterioration between inspection sites. As a result, it minimizes the number of inspection sites needed and accelerates problem resolution, offering a more efficient and precise way to manage process-related issues.

articleTitle: A Super-Resolution Method for Non-Uniform Mesh Data based on Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Mesh data is vital for simulating complex systems in engineering and scientific computation. Higher mesh resolution enhances accuracy and convergence speed but incurs significant computational costs. To address this, we present the Non-Uniform Mesh Super-Resolution Neural Network (NMSRN), a deep learning-based method that reconstructs low-resolution meshes into high-resolution ones, improving data accuracy and optimizing resource usage. NMSRN integrates an autoencoder with an Efficient Sub-Pixel Convolutional Neural Network (ESPCN) for enhanced feature learning and modular training, boosting reusability and adaptability. Comparative experiments on a 2D low-temperature plasma simulation demonstrate NMSRN’s superior accuracy and generalization. Additionally, we investigate fine-tuning strategies for efficiently adapting pre-trained models to new mesh super-resolution tasks.

articleTitle: Stuck-At and At-Speed Interconnect Tests for 3D-IC
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of integrated circuits, it is much more difficult to reduce the chip size, the 3D-IC technique is a promising approach to solve this problem by stacking dies fabricated by different foundries with the most efficient technology node. But only the concerns about heat dissipation, yield, and test cost are solved then the 3D-IC can be large-scale commercial used<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. When the chips are stacked together, the data switch between different dies mainly relies on the interconnect between the stacked dies such as micro-bumps, a cluster of TSVs and so on. So the interconnect test plays a important role in the stacked chip defects screening by adding effective design-for-test (DFT) features to fully test the interconnects. In this paper, a die wrapper register (DWR) structure based on IEEE1838 standard [2] is introduced which can be used to test not only the stuck-at fault, but also the transition fault of the interconnects. As for the at-speed test, the synchronous OCC(on-chip-clock) logic is also used to test the register-to-register at-speed inter-die path. Depending on the specific defects that need to be detected, the SCAN/JTAG switch logic used in the design can be configured. So the DWRs can also function as boundary scan cells during Know-Good-Die (KGD) test stage by connecting the DWRs to the JTAG network. And the use of scan logic for interconnect test can support fault diagnose which plays an important role in improving yield of 3D-IC.

articleTitle: Polysilicon trench etch in memory device
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the increase of memory density, the small cell size brings many key challenges such as mask selectivity and profile control due to the reduction of critical dimension and higher aspect ratio. To face these challenges, a cyclic etching process consisting of etching step, break through step, and oxidation treatment step has been proposed and applied to polysilicon etching in memory flow. The effects of RF power, gas ratio, temperature, and pressure on etching characteristics are discussed. Research has found that the degree of anisotropic profile control depends on the etching rate and the physical and chemical reaction balance of thin film deposition, sputtering, and etching. The selectivity of the hard mask is related to the BRF power and the Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/HBr gas ratio during the etching process. This will provide a good reference for the etching of capacitors in the next generation memory device.

articleTitle: Inline Non-Contacting Measurement of Effective Work Function
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: An inline method for effective work function measurement using a non-contacting Kelvin probe-based instrument shall enable engineers to quickly reach an optimal metal gate process condition that shall result in the desired Vt value, thus to effectively accelerate the development progress. In this paper, the theory of this method and the mechanism of the instrument are discussed, accompanied by some example measurement results as well.

articleTitle: Backside Chipping Improvement Study On Hybrid Bonding Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The next generation of electronic devices such as micro-dimensional integration is playing a more and more important role and direct wafer bonding (fusion bonding and hybrid bonding of Cu/Dielectric damascene patterned surfaces) has been getting extra attention due to the capability of enhancing system performance. After bonding, two kinds of diamond abrasive processes, namely wafer backside grinding and edge trimming, are normally processed to realize significant Si thickness reduction. In edge trimming, due to the high rotation speed of diamond blade working at the wafer edge, the chipping and delamination at the wafer edge is easily suffered. According to the damage region caused by edge trimming, chipping can be defined as Front Side Chipping(FSC) and Back Side Chipping(BSC). In this paper, the mechanisms of the formation of BSC between fusion bonding and hybrid bonding is discussed. In addition, blade selection and trimming parameters optimization is investigated. The main parameters of blade include the abrasive grit size(Factor1), the resin adhesive(Factor2) and the proportion of chip pockets(Factor3). For the trimming parameters, feed speed of blade and cutting depth of wafer were detail investigated. The results indicated with a smaller abrasive size of diamond between 5-8μm, according to adjustment of cutting depth, better BSC performance can be achieved.

articleTitle: A Model Using Plasma Enhanced Vapor Chemical Deposition of Silicon Nitride Side Walls
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the process of chip manufacturing, the side wall plays an important role in controlling the channel length of CMOS devices and reducing the short channel effect. The side wall of silicon nitride deposited by CVD is usually used as the side wall in the device, which has a blocking effect on most matter atoms, increases the width of the gate and drain LDD region.In this paper, partial differential equation simulation software was used to model the process of CVD deposition of silicon nitride side wall, completing the whole process from plasma modeling to surface deposition, and studying the influence of input process parameters on the morphology of the side wall.

articleTitle: Evolution Mechanism of Copper Grains in Advanced Interconnect Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In dual-damascene interconnect applications, the decreasing copper concentration and lower current/voltage in electrochemical plating pose challenges to Cu grain evolution. This paper investigates Cu grain growth in low-Cu plating solutions using two types of seed layers. Results show that larger original grains in CuMn seed layers lead to separation from the electroplated layer. During self-annealing, grains evolve vertically from the bottom upward due to seed stress, and horizontally from the wafer center outward under grain boundary forces. Moreover, precise control of current density can effectively optimize the growth behavior of Cu grains, thereby improving device performance.

articleTitle: Z2-FET Memory with Both Flash and DRAM Modes
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this study, we develop a novel memory device based on Z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-FET. Our memory device exhibits dual-mode operation as either flash or DRAM (dynamic random access memory) under different bias conditions. The functionality is validated through TCAD simulations. The flash memory mode is achieved by integrating an engineered gate dielectric for charge storage in the Z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-FET. In flash mode, data readout is innovatively achieved by applying voltage from the source in order to avoid triggering the transient feedback used in DRAM mode. In DRAM mode, the charge stored in gate capacitor is read out through feedback mechanism. The flash and DRAM modes demonstrate non-volatile and fast access speed characteristics, respectively. Eventually, a process based on fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) substrate is developed to fabricate the dual-mode Z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-FET memory which is further subjected to preliminary measurements.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Anisotropic Dielectric Constant of Package Material Considering the Fiber-Weave Effect
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The anisotropic nature of the dielectric constant (Dk) in package materials is notably impacted by the presence of glass fiber weaves, resulting in distinct Dk values between the XY plane and the Z direction. This study presents a theoretical analysis and numerical calculation of the directional variations in dielectric constants induced by glass cloth fibers. These calculations are further validated through EM cavity resonator simulations, confirming their accuracy. For the first time, it is conclusively demonstrated that in substrate materials containing glass fibers, the equivalent dielectric constant in the plane is higher than that in the perpendicular direction. This finding offers significant guidance for the design of high-frequency and high-speed electronic products.

articleTitle: Interpretable Virtual Metrology-Driven Adaptive dEWMA Control for Nonlinear Semiconductor Process Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Precise process control is essential in semiconductor manufacturing to maintain product quality and reduce variability. This paper proposes an adaptive Run-to-Run (R2R) control algorithm that integrates a virtual metrology model with interpretable machine learning techniques. The algorithm combines Accumulated Local Effects (ALE) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to guide parameter adjustments in a double Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (dEWMA) controller. ALE gradients are utilized to refine adjustment directions and magnitudes, while SHAP values prioritize critical variables, enabling dynamic and precise control of nonlinear processes across batch runs. Comparative studies with traditional EWMA and dEWMA controllers highlight the proposed method's superior prediction accuracy and control performance, providing a robust and intelligent solution for advanced semiconductor process optimization.

articleTitle: Symmetry and Anisotropy in Wafer Deformation: Their Effect on Alignment Signal Degradation
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: To minimize overlay errors, precise alignment is essential. However, wafer warpages caused by chemical-mechanical polishing or high-temperature processing can severely compromise alignment accuracy. This work extends our previous work by developing a more comprehensive model of alignment mark behavior under wafer deformation. Using the finite-difference time-domain method, we evaluate how diffraction signals vary under different deformation modes. Our results demonstrate that asymmetric and parallel direction deformations have a more noticeable impact on alignment marks' diffraction signals. This provides valuable insights for resolving warpage-related wafer rejection and designing novel alignment marks that are resistant to wafer warpage.

articleTitle: Research on EOS Damage of Chips Caused by Abnormal CPU Power-off Sequence
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Recently, an issue that the product was not powered on has been claimed by our customers. As it has been identified as caused by a chip malfunction, a series of failure analysis was conducted on the failed chip. The test results of automatic test equipment (ATE) indicated that a short circuit abnormality existed in the power pin, VDDQ1_1P1, which was consistent with the I-V test results. No obvious abnormalities were found in the appearance inspection, scanning acoustic tomography (SAT), X-ray and other non-destructive testing. Subsequently, failure localization was carried out on the short circuited power pin and it was observed that the abnormal point was located in the DDR module inside the die, with obvious burn marks. After investigation, it was found that electrical over stress (EOS) damage was caused by abnormal power-off sequence. According to the circuit and power-off waveform analysis, adjusting the CPU power-off sequence to ensure that the VDD voltage of DrMOS is last powered off, should be adopted as the solution.

articleTitle: Highly Effective and Flexible Device Designs for High-Voltage ESD Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, ESD protection structures are studied in response to the growing demands driven by the rapid development of high-voltage (HV) BCD platforms and HV analog products. ESDPNP devices, featuring a guardring stacked design and flexible implantation combination, show great promise as HV ESD protection solutions. These devices can be modulated with trigger voltage ranging from 15 to 100V by precisely tuning device internal dimensions. Additionally, high failure current (2-4A) are achieved by adjusting the collector doping type. The thermal failure mechanism and potential performance deterioration are discussed, providing guidance for future improvements in device design.

articleTitle: A Novel Dynamic Hypergraph Attention Framework for the Prediction of Removal Rate in Chemical Mechanical Polishing Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of machine learning technology, numerous algorithms have been employed to enhance the prediction accuracy of material removal rate (MRR). In this paper, a novel prediction framework is introduced based on a dynamic hypergraph attention mechanism, providing accurate MRR predictions. This approach utilizes the multi-level attention mechanism within the hypergraph architecture to effectively capture the relationships between nodes and hyperedges in the polishing machine, enabling precise MRR predictions, while maintaining a low data processing cost. Experimental results show that our method achieved an RMSE of 1.42 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.963, outperforming current state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: Ceria Polishing Abrasives with Enhanced Dispersion Stability Across Wide pH Range
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Ceria slurries demonstrate a high material removal rate and significant selectivity between SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, making them widely utilized in the domain of chemical mechanical polishing. Those with high dispersion stability were highly sought after, as aggregation significantly reduces polishing efficiency and surface quality. This study proposes, for the first time, that the surface modification of CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with polyacrylic acid (PAA), sulfuric acid (SA), and Akm-0530 could yield a new polishing abrasive that exhibits high stability across a broad range of pH values. Importantly, these modified CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> abrasives demonstrate a specific response to variations in external pH, enabling the pH of the polishing slurry to remain stable at approximately 3-4. The crystal structure and valence state distribution of the modified CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> abrasives are characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), respectively. These modified CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> abrasives possess the potential for application in chemical mechanical polishing.

articleTitle: Machine Learning to Model and Predict Layout Dependent Effects on 55nm Low Power Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Layout-dependent effects (LDEs) play a critical role in determining the performance of field-effect transistors (FETs), influencing key parameters such as threshold voltage (Vt), mobility, and saturation current (Idsat). These effects can significantly degrade the performance of mixed-signal integrated circuits fabricated on a 55nm low power platform. In this paper, we investigate two major LDEs: the length of diffusion (LOD) effect and the well proximity effect (WPE). A machine learning (ML) algorithm is developed to model and predict these effects, using testing data from devices under test (DUT). By employing a well-trained deep neural network (DNN) model, we analyze the FET characteristics (Vt and Idsat) and compare the results with those derived from both BSIM4 compact model SPICE simulations and Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations. Our results highlight the effectiveness of the ML-based approach as a powerful tool for modeling and predicting LDEs in the context of integrated circuit manufacturing.

articleTitle: A Design Stucture of Three Axis MEMS Accelerometer with Low Cross-Axis Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and characterization of a three axis capacitive MEMS accelerometer comprised of two proof masses. By using FEM (Finite Element Method), we analyzed the influence of spring beams on the performance of the accelerometer, especially the cross-axis sensitivity. Critical parameters of spring beams have been found. And differentially detecting capacitors are used to achieve low cross-axis sensitivity. All cross-axis sensitivities are lower than 0.05%. The geometric dimensions of each proof-mass are selected at 1×0.9×0.05 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Self-Limited Behavior Study on Dielectric Quasi-Atomic Layer Etching for Selectivity Achievement
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Atomic layer etching (ALE) has attracted wide attention in the continuous downscaling progress of semiconductor devices. It is achieved by cyclic process of surface modification (deposition step) and subsequent removal of modified layer (etch step). The self-limited feature is the key for ALE to fulfill atomic-scale etch precision and high material selectivity. In this work, self-limited behavior was explored in dielectric ALE with fluorocarbon plasma. The effect of ion energy was studied by pure argon sputtering on different substrates. The etch behaviors of silicon oxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and silicon nitride (SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) at different surface states were compared to provide an insight to selectivity achievement. Moreover, the LF-assisted deposition was proved to be valuable for realizing high selectivity, promoting wide application of ALE in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Mechanism and Effect of 4-Level RF Pulsing on Etching Process in Advanced Node
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Dry etching is a science and technology about plasma behavior controlling and it directly affects the performance of IC device, especially in advanced node. However, current method of plasma precise controlling is still lacking. Here, it reports a novel 4-level RF pulsing function. Through multiple combinations of source power and bias power within each pulse, it can independently control radical density, ion bombardment and power off pump out degree. It is helpful to gain higher selectivity and sidewall protection in high-aspect-ratio (HAR).This new advanced RF feature in ICP provide a better process tuning solution for some key applications.

articleTitle: Design for LDMOS Device Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The LDMOS design involves physical-based TCAD simulations and multiple rounds of experiment to calibrate models and optimize parameters. However, due to limited experimental data, the calibration of models and tuning of parameters become complex and time-consuming. To address these challenges, we propose a neural network (NN) model trained via transfer learning to replace and refine traditional design routine. The NN is trained on TCAD simulation data and fine-tuned with a small set of measured data to ensure accurate performance predictions. This AI-TCAD methodology significantly shortens design cycles, reduces costs, and is adaptable for optimizing other IC devices.

articleTitle: Modeling of NTD Resist Shrinkage Based on Spring-Mass System
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The shrinkage effect of negative tone development (NTD) process is a major factor influencing the accuracy of resist models. As a result, incorporating a resist model that accounts for this shrinkage is crucial for precise lithography simulations in NTD process. This paper presents a practical workflow of building a resist model considering shrinkage effect in NTD process. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively captures this phenomenon, which provides a possibility for significantly improving the prediction accuracy of NTD simulations.

articleTitle: Study on the Efficiency Enhancement of Chemical Mechanical Polishing of Gallium Nitride by Acetic Acid
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study investigates the role of acetic acid (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>COOH) as a pH regulator in ceria-based slurries for chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) of gallium nitride (GaN) thin films. Through a series of experiments, it was discovered that the incorporation of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>COOH significantly enhances the material removal rate (MRR) up to 495.2 nm/h, representing a 70% increase compared to nitric acid. The resulting GaN surfaces exhibited exceptional smoothness with a surface roughness (Sq) of 0.07 nm. The findings offer promising insights for optimizing CMP processes for GaN applications in the semiconductor industry.

articleTitle: A Diffusion-Based Approach to Wafer Defect Image Generation in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Accurate defect detection in semiconductor manufacturing is crucial but often hindered by data scarcity and labeling costs. To address this, we develop a latent diffusion model that generates wafer defect images with specified defect types and locations using mask-based control and textual prompts, ensuring real backgrounds simultaneously. By training defect detection models on this augmented dataset with our generated images, we achieved a 15.4% increase in Precision, 16.5% in Recall, and 16.3% in F1-score over baseline methods, validating the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: A Sige Channel Gate-All-Around Transistor Fabricated Using Novel Cyclic Self-Limiting Wet Etching Combined with SI Removal Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, a novel SiGe channel gate-all-around (GAA) transistor using a cyclic self-limiting wet etching process combined with Si removal process after dummy gate removal in the mainstream FinFET process is demonstrated in detail. The width of SiGe channel is narrowed from 20 nm to 6.5 nm and its mole fraction of Ge of SiGe channel can be increased from 31.8% to ~40%. Meanwhile, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> of 382 μA/μm is obtained at V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> = V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> = -0.8V, with I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ratio of ~5.5e5 and SS of 76 mV/dec. These results prove that this novel process provides a potential solution to prepare the SiGe channel GAA transistor.

articleTitle: Optimizing Polysilicon Deposition to Reduce Bump Defects in CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Defects in polysilicon films critically influence the performance and yield of CMOS devices during IC manufacturing. Through our practical production experience, we identified that a substantial number of bump defects emerged on the surface of the deposited u-poly layer, which had a detrimental effect on subsequent processing, device performance, and overall product yield. In this study, we characterized the thin films and investigated the mechanisms responsible for defect formation. By optimizing pressure and gas flow rates, significant improvements can be achieved in addressing the defect-related issues.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Monolithic CFET by Backside Enhanced Contact with C-type Source/Drain Contact Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, to optimized source/drain (S/D) contact in monolithic CFET, the backside enhanced contact (BSEC) technology is proposed and investigated by TCAD simulation, which can be used to form C-type S/D contact. Compared with the conventional L-type contact of common drain in monolithic CFET, the on-current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>) of bottom PFET with C-type S/D contact shows a 25.4% increase as the contact resistivity is 3e-9 Ω•cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> of top NFET has little affects. Furthermore, the C-type S/D contact based on BSEC technology is conducive to further improving bottom PFET’s driving performance, relieving the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> mismatch between PFET and NFET for monolithic CFET, and optimizing the transient characteristics of CFET inverter.

articleTitle: Methodology on Adaptive Iterative Step in Inverse Lithography
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The influence of iteration step on mask optimization performance in inverse lithography technology (ILT) is studied, and an adaptive iteration step algorithm is designed. A large iteration step may result in inability to converge, while a small step may lead to slow convergence and the possibility of getting stuck in a local optimal solution. Adaptive step in real-time based on changes of cost can balance efficiency and mask optimization effect. This method may contribute to the wider application of ILT in photolithography technology.

articleTitle: Selective Reflector Assisted Thermal budget Decrease
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper reports a selective reflection plate, which can reduce the target thermal budget by reducing the dwell time in the process of spike annealing.

articleTitle: Automated Layout Design for High Frequency Integrated Circuits Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) based automated layout design procedure for high frequency integrated circuits, and demonstrate its feasibility on low noise amplifier (LNA) architectures at process node 40nm Si CMOS. Given a pre-optimized design and its corresponding device blocks, a proper layout solution can be generated within 1 hour. The post-simulation result of the generated layout has a loss of no more than 5% in performance (Gain, Noise Figure, etc.) compared to pre-simulation results. The algorithm is based on Reinforcement Learning (RL) Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and implemented by Actor-Critic framework. The placement is done by optimizing positions and directions of each device block, routing is accomplished using A-star algorithm. The automation procedure is highly modularized and portable between different design environments and different process nodes, exhibiting great potential in solving complex high frequency placement & routing (P&R) problems.

articleTitle: Study on Tungsten (W) Filling Void Improvement with Chamfered Gate Profiles
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: High-K/Metal Gate (HKMG) is one of the most remarkable innovations that enable scaling of Integrated Circuits (ICs). In the HKMG gate-last approach, dummy poly gate is removed and then Work Function Metal (WFM) layers are deposited, and finally the space is filled with Tungsten (W) using Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD). Void-free W CVD has become challenging with High Aspect Ratio (HAR) brought by continuous device dimension scaling down. The existence of W voids results in increased risk of High-K exposure, which can potentially lead to Fin damage in the subsequent W etch back process and ultimately device failure. One way to eliminate W voids is to form a chamfered profile prior to W filling, which could be realized by pulling back SiN spacer at the dummy poly gate removal step or WFM during WFM BARC etch. In this paper, the two chamfered profile approaches — chamfered spacer (SP) approach and chamfered WFM approach — are studied systematically through virtual fabrication method. The impact of chamfered profile height and width on void volume and device yield are investigated. We found that shallow chamfered depth improves W filling without any voids forming, while deep chamfered profile leads to large voids instead. A void-free metal gate is beneficial for low RC delay, and with the same chamfered profile condition, SP approach has better RC performance compared the WFM approach. Through device simulation, the void-free metal gate was proven to have a stronger control on channel with a resulting boost in device performance.

articleTitle: Effect of High Temperature Furnace Anneal to Element Diffusion in SIO2-SI3N4 Stacks
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Aiming at sloped profile post lateral etch of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers within the 5 tiers of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(ON) stacks, we added 700/800°C furnace anneal for 30 min in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> atmosphere of ON stacks before etch. Compared with non-anneal ON stacks, N concentration in SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> increased and distribution is more uniform as expected. Furthermore, H content in SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers also decreased from 2E20 to 1.5E20 atoms/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which is benefit to channel stability. SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> later etch process was then performed on the post annealed ON stacks, slope-type profile was disappeared which prove N non-uniform diffusion result in sloped profile, provides valuable insights for the development of 3D DRAM technologies.

articleTitle: Application of System in Package Technology in Satellite Internet
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In recent years, the digital divide of the "No Internet" population has attracted more and more social attention. The construction of satellite Internet is an important means to solve the digital divide problem. In particular, the Starlink program, proposed and being implemented by Elon Musk's SpaceX, has been a huge success. People are full of expectations for the future of satellite Internet, and anything is possible. In view of the development trend of miniaturization, lightweight and integration of satellite Internet phased array antenna, we optimize the traditional RF digital transceiver module based on SiP technology, which greatly reduces the volume and weight, and solves the problem of thermal mismatch simultaneously.

articleTitle: Circuit Design and Sneak Path Current Analysis of 28NM 1T4R RRAM Memory IP
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In recent years, with the fast advancement of emerging technologies, resistive random-access memory (RRAM) has emerged as one of the most promising memory technologies due to its compact size, low power consumption, fast read and write speed. Building upon the traditional one-transistor-one-resistor (1T1R) array, this paper proposes an innovative one-transistor-four-resistor (1T4R) array architecture that increases the integration density of the array. A 16×16 scale 1T4R memory IP has been designed on a commercial 28nm RRAM technology platform, and the impact of sneak path current on the array operation has been verified through simulation and testing. Additionally, a novel evaluation method has been proposed to analyze the relationship between sneak path current, array size, operating voltage, and the resistance value of the low-resistance state, where the feasibility and advantages of the 1T4R architecture in RRAM array design have been verified through simulations.

articleTitle: White-Pixel Performance Improvement on CIS VIISta Trident Application
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the CMOS image sensor manufacturing process, the pinging layer in the pixel area is particularly sensitive and prone to metal contamination. This paper demonstrated a novel method to improve white-pixel (WP) performance through enhancements in the implantation process beyond hardware in MRK and TPFG. Through a series of experiments, feasible experimental conditions were obtained to highly improve the performance of WP under both high and low light yield test conditions. We have successfully helped customer to improve the yield on the road of pixel improvement.

articleTitle: An Investigation into the Optimization of Photolithography Process for Silicon Nitride Devices on the fab's 12-inch Production Line
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The research and development of low-loss SiN silicon photonic devices are still in the laboratory stage, with only a handful of tape-outs having been conducted in 8-inch fabs. We are pioneering the development of SiN silicon photonic devices on 12-inch production line, thereby establishing a robust foundation for mass production. This study primarily focuses on the photolithography process utilized in the production of SiN devices [1], and investigates the impact of various factors, including stepper types, development conditions, temperature, and anti-reflection coatings. The photolithography of SiN devices mainly encounters problems photoresist (PR) residue and high line width roughness (LWR). It is found that when using a KrF [2] stepper, changing the development method has minimal impact on the photoresist residue. Raising the temperature from 120°C to 130°C can effectively mitigate the issue of residue in small line width patterns, however, residue defects persist in large line width patterns. Replacing the bottom anti-reflection coating (BARC) [3], [4] with bottom anti-reflection coating (TARC) can effectively improve PR residue, nonetheless, the issue of high LWR [5] remains pronounced. Switching to an Arf stepper [2] and utilizing both BARC and dielectric anti-reflection coating (DARC) can effectively reduce LWR. This study provides significant guidance for the exploitation of photolithography process in the production of SiN devices within 12-inch fab lines, thereby facilitating the advancement towards mass production of silicon optical devices.

articleTitle: Use Damascus CMP to fabricate IGZO transistor in advanced Dram technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: IGZO is a new kind channel material that possible be used in the most advanced Dram technology, with its most attractive capability of extremely low I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> and long retention time as transistor, eighter in 1T1C structure or in 2T0C structure. For the first time, we fabricated a vertical transistor that consist of IGZO/AlO/IZO materials on pattern wafer by Damascus CMP method. To achieve a good post CMP dishing, we tested different kinds of slurry and finally chosen an acid and contained H2O2 slurry.

articleTitle: The Optimization of the Gate Polysilicon Deposition Process for Power MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: During the fabrication of Shielded-Gate Trench MOSFETs (SGT MOSFETs), the trench associated with the gate is filled with polysilicon. Polysilicon is essential to the performance and stability of integrated circuits in semiconductor manufacture. Poor quality polysilicon film leads to the degradation of device performance and may cause circuit failure. This study investigates the polysilicon film quality of trenches under different processing conditions in two types of furnace systems: UPOLY and DPOLY. In UPOLY system, the results of experiment revealed that temperature has the most significant influence on film quality. Within the temperature range of 580-535 °C, lower temperatures resulted in better film quality. This result was validated in DPOLY system. This work provides guidance for obtaining optimal processing conditions for the growth of polysilicon in filled trenches.

articleTitle: Process Window Optimization for Gate Etch Process of 2D NAND
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Two dimensional (2D) NAND has been used in applications such as industrial control systems and automotive electronics. Manufacturers working on further scale traditional planar NAND face significant challenges in processing high aspect ratio (HAR) structures. This paper focuses on the gate etch process of 2D NAND, presenting findings from a systematic investigation conducted using SEMulator3D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, a 3D predictive modeling software. The analysis reveals that the formation mechanisms of two primary defects during the gate etch, active area (AA) pitting and fence defects, are intricately linked to the control of oxide-nitride-oxide (ONO) spacer height in the control gate (CG), ONO and floating gate (FG) etch processes. Furthermore, the defect process window is explored, highlighting the critical importance of both ONO/poly selectivity and poly etch amount control. Ensuring a proper balance is essential for managing spacer height effectively. During actual gate etch process tuning, pattern loading emerges as the most challenging issue, including the trade-offs between pitting, fencing and profile loading across different patterns. Effective strategies have been implemented to optimize the process window. The findings of this investigation not only reveal the key lesson learned for the control of AA pitting and fence defects, but also provide guidance for appropriate gate etch recipe design and process window optimization.

articleTitle: Comparison of simulation and actual test results and selection of molding material in Flip-Chip Package
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The warping problem has become more and more important to the reliablity of solder joint with the development of packaging technology, and how to accurately predict package warping has attracted a lot of attention. In this paper, the effect of EMC(Epoxy molding compound) type on the warping of FC(Flip-Chip) package are investigated using Ansys software. And the strip model of Flip Chip Chip Scale Package was conducted according to the real design. Besides, the warping of strip for FC package is important to the product yield, the warping behavior of real products was compared with simulation results. Results suggested that reasonable consideration of EMC’s shrinkage rate in products can make simulation and testing results more consistent.

articleTitle: A 10.2-to-14.82-GHz Low-Phase-Noise All-Digital Phase-Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents a subsampling bang-bang all-digital phase-locked loop (SS-BB-ADPLL) implemented in the TSMC 40nm process. The proposed PLL architecture replaces conventional time-to-digital converter (TDC) with a bang-bang phase detector (BBPD), effectively reducing circuit complexity. It also utilizes a transformer-feedback dual-core digitally controlled oscillator, which further reduces phase noise and achieves low jitter performance. The design achieves a measured root mean square (RMS) jitter of 196.8 fs in integer-N mode and 707.7 fs in fractional-N mode, while demonstrating a frequency tuning range from 10.2 GHz to 14.82 GHz.

articleTitle: The Influence of Writing Pulse on Memory Window of FE-FinFET
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, we research the storage characteristics of ferroelectric transistors by experiments and simulations. Firstly, the FE-FinFET (fin field-effect transistor) with 9nm-HZO ferroelectric dielectric layer is used to research the influence of the amplitude and width of writing pulse on the storage characteristics, and we have a simple analysis. In addition, we simulate the experimental process with technology computer aided design (TCAD) models and obtain the same results.

articleTitle: Using Double-EPI Structure to Solve the Problems Caused by High Process Temperature Requirements
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In some BCD processes, if the annealing temperature of NBL and DNW processes is too high, it will cause the upward and downward diffusion of NBL, and the p-type layer of sub will also expand upward. Due to this, it will bring many problems, such as the need for deepe substrate layers, and upper silicon layers. This article uses a double-epi structure and inject additional DNW between two epi processes, thereby reducing the temperature required for thermal and avoiding the above situation. This article improves the thermal process and ion implantation of a specific BCD process. Satisfactory results were obtained through TCAD simulation, which matched the inherent properties and reduced the thermal diffusion temperature and ion diffusion.

articleTitle: A Common Building Block for Media SoC Analog Test on Advantest V93000 ATE Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Media System-on-Chip (SoC) is specialized integrated circuits designed to handle multimedia tasks such as audio, video, and image processing. And its analog components are tested using Automated Test Equipment (ATE) for high precision in signal generation, error analysis, and parametric measurements. To address the complexity of current devices, a Common Building Block (CBB) framework was developed for efficient ATE test program generation. This framework supports ADC/DAC tests, loopback tests, and integrates with the V93000 WSMX board for enhanced performance on SMT8.

articleTitle: An Efficient Automatic Design Method for LDMOS Devices Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this study, an efficient automatic design method is proposed for laterally-diffused metal-oxide semiconductor (LDMOS) devices. This method integrates Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) model to automatically design device structure parameters that meet target requirements in a multi-dimensional design space. To comprehensively evaluate the performance of this method, the performance of integrating PSO algorithm is compared with that of Bayesian Optimization (BO) algorithm. The results show that PSO algorithm performs excellently in device design and takes much less computing resource and run time than the BO algorithm. This proposed method provides an efficient and intelligent new approach for LDMOS devices design, laying the foundation for the design and process development of power devices.

Index Terms: Laterally Diffused Metal Oxide Semiconductor Device

articleTitle: Emerging Trends and Advances in Computing-in-Memory: A Software-Hardware Co-Design Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Computing-in-memory (CIM) has emerged as a promising solution to the memory bottleneck in deep neural network (DNN) acceleration, yet maximizing its potential requires careful software-hardware co-design. This paper systematically examines key co-optimization techniques for CIM architectures, including quantization, sparsity, compact models, and decomposition. The analysis also explores how software stacks can effectively bridge the gap between high-level DNN frameworks and CIM hardware primitives. Finally, this work identifies unresolved challenges across the hardware-software stack and propose concrete research directions to advance this emerging paradigm.

articleTitle: Understanding Electromigration Failure Modes in Cu Interconnects with Different Line Widths
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper investigated the electromigration (EM) of Cu interconnects with different line widths. It was found that EM performance of wide lines was worse than narrow lines due to bimodal failures, where the early failure mode is void under via. Comprehensive testing and failure analyses (FA) were carried out to understand the mechanisms. Slit voids between Cu and capping layer in line ends adjacent to vias prior to EM stress and via bottom to Cu line interface cleanness were identified as the two root causes of the early fails. Modulation of failure modes by different processes was achieved. The early failure mode was suppressed after process optimization.

articleTitle: Investigating the etch Performance of Zirconium-Based Photoresist for Direct Silicon Oxide Etching
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work we investigated one step direct silicone oxide etching using a novel zirconium based photoresist instead of the multilayer method commonly used in the semiconductor industries, It’s cost and time effective and also minimizes the chances of error. After optimizing important parameters including Pressure, Bias power and ICP power and other etch conditions we obtained selectivity of resist to silicon oxide of over 18.8 to 1 with 97% resist still left on the surface. This is much higher than the selectivity’s of 1 to 4 reported in the literature for the etches of silicon oxide using conventional e-beam resists. The etch depth obtained after 180 seconds is about 866 nm with an etch rate up to 288 nm/min. Overall, our results suggest that a zirconium resist could be used in a simplified process without a hard mask or trilayer setup and still get deep etch depths. This may be an opportunity for useful process simplification.

articleTitle: A Study of Photoresist Residue Defect Induced by Develop Condition
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As the critical size of semiconductor devices decreases below 40nm, the manufacturing processes for integrated circuits will encounter increasingly severe challenges. The complexity of these processes results in a significant reduction in tolerance for defects. During the development of the wafer with oxide substrate, we encountered a Photoresist (PR) residue defect that could not be eliminated using conventional process flows. This PR residue constitutes a critical defect that adversely affects product yield and reliability, necessitating a clear understanding of its mechanism and effective reduction strategy. Although the factory can reduce PR residue to a lower level by changing PR or optimizing the development process, the defect mechanism is unknown, and require further study. An interesting phenomenon observed during experiments revealed that variations in layout, particularly when large areas of PR are opened under the same mask transmission, lead to different PR residue defect count. Under identical development conditions and mask transmission, experiments were conducted with both centralized and dispersed openings of the PR. The results demonstrated that PR residue only happened in areas where the PR was opened in sets, while the dispersed openings remained free of residue. Based on these findings, we can anticipate PR residue defects during the early design phase of product development through careful layout planning. This early prediction, made during the GDS phase of product development, significantly conserves resources and capitalizes on valuable opportunities. The research presented in this paper establishes a foundation for reducing PR residue defects, thereby enhancing product quality and reliability.

articleTitle: Research on the Root Cause of THB Failure of Large Size Package Chip to Improve Reliability
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the root cause and mechanism of short failure of large size packaged chip in THB (Temperature Humidity Bias Life Test) are analyzed.
