We find that the failure mechanism of short is due to the introduction of aluminum-containing foreign matter in the substrate processing process, which produces cracks and provides an effective path for Cu migration. Under the conditions of high temperature, high humidity and voltage bias of THB, the electromigration of Cu ions occurs between the copper hole and the copper plane, thus forming a bridge conduction. Meanwhile, our analysis identifies the source of the foreign matter. The risk of foreign matter introduction is reduced by process protection. The ability to detect defects is improved by adjusting the electrical measurement parameters. The spark voltage is tightened from 10V to 2V, which can effectively detect the micro-short and the near-short defect mode. Moreover, the effectiveness of the countermeasures is verified, and the reliability of the chip is obviously improved.

articleTitle: Depth Uniformity of Silicon and Dielectric Trenches Etching for the Burried Wordline of Novel Memory
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Advanced integrated circuit device structures drive advances in advanced process methods and precision equipment. We have explored two ideas for simultaneously etching different substances to the same depth in a small-size deep trench buried wordline etching process for alternating silicon and dielectric layers of a new memory, which achieves both good control of silicon column morphology in the compensated mode and small-size deep trench with good depth uniformity by optimizing the size of the trench opening.

articleTitle: Near-Zero Residue High-Reliability Novel Solder Paste for Electronics
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Flux residues, which remain on assembly boards after reflow, can cause electrical and mechanical connection problems that impact the long-term reliability performance of solder joints. Near-zero residue (NZR) soldering technology, using an active reducing atmosphere such as formic gas or hydrogen, has been known for many years and is becoming an active area of research. High-reliability novel lead-free solder alloy 90.6Sn3.2Ag0.7Cu5.5Sb, designated as Indalloy®276, is known for its high reliability with wide service temperature capabilities. Indalloy®276 preforms are applied to specific applications in semiconductor industry that require high reliability and no residue. However, preforms can’t achieve the proper tackiness to hold a component during reflow, resulting in defects such as tombstoning. In this manuscript, a novel solder paste with Indalloy®276 and a specially-designed binder was developed and tested. The soldering performance testing included printability, wetting, voids, residue content, and shear strength of the created solder joints. These tests were conducted and compared with regular no-clean Indalloy®276 solder paste.

articleTitle: Optimizing Photoresist Coating Processes with Computational Fluid Dynamics and Taguchi Design of Experiments
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The uniformity of photoresist film thickness is crucial in microelectronics manufacturing, as it impacts device consistency and yield. Accurate prediction and control of the distribution of photoresist on wafers are the keys to achieve a uniform coating. The traditional liquid film flow model typically predicts only the average thickness of the photoresist, limiting their effectiveness. In this study, we present an OpenFOAM-based hydromechanical simulation method for the photoresist spin coating process. This method enables the simulation of the photoresist distribution on the rotating wafer under varying process conditions. Furthermore, we employed the Taguchi experimental design techniques to optimize the coating process, identifying the best operating conditions for achieving uniform photoresist coating.

articleTitle: Research on Reducing Leakage in 2T Sonos Embedded Flash by Preamorphization Implant
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, a method of reducing leakage in a 2 Mb embedded nonvolatile memory using 2T-SONOS (Silicon-Oxide-Nitride-Oxide-Silicon) by preamorphization implant is proposed and verified. Although SONOS memory has excellent performance in storing charge and resisting defects, we still find single-bit failures due to leakage in the SONOS region. By high energy Ge implant, the ONO boundary in the SONOS region of the floating gate can be reduced due to process fluctuations, stress or other reasons to increase its uniformity, reduce the leakage electrons generated in the floating gate, thus reducing the tunnel thermal electrons generated by horizontal accumulation, and finally reduce the leakage caused by the accumulation of charge in the nitride layer of electricity storage. The most intuitive effect is that parameters of WAT test related to cell leakage can be reduced by 5% generally, and the maximum reduction can up to 20%. And CKBD/iCKBD failure efficiency decreases to a certain extent.

articleTitle: SiC Etch with Inductively Coupled Plasma for Power Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the next-generation power device applications, SiC materials with high thermal stability and wide bandgap exhibit outstanding performance, leading to a growing market share. Inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etch is one of the key processes in SiC device fabrication, directly impacting the electrical performance and yield of power devices. In this study, the latest 8-inch ICP etching machine developed by AMEC was utilized on SiC etching, achieving high etch rate, high selectivity, and excellent profiles. By optimizing the ratios of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and Ar gases, SiC etch rate exceeding 7500 Å/min were achieved, with a SiC/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> selectivity approaching 6. Furthermore, it was observed that the top critical dimension (TCD) size is closely correlated with the chemical etching process. Using enthetic passivation gas such as SiF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> can effectively protect the sidewall from the chemical etching during SiC etch. During the pattern transfer etch process, vertical sidewall profiles and smooth bottom rounded corners were achieved by adjusting ICP parameters. These innovations provide important insights for further optimization of SiC etch processes and enhancement of power device performance.

articleTitle: Investigation and Optimization of Zener Diode in Advanced Process Node
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Zener diode is widely used in IC design, and its reversed leakage current is an important electrical parameter. As space technology advances, the P/N junction depth of smaller size platforms is shallower and more concentrated, resulting in a larger leakage current and a more near-surface breakdown location for zener diodes. In this paper, the impact of process variations on the leakage current is investigated, and a new approach is proposed to reduce the leakage current by adding a p-type dose injection.

articleTitle: Sym3™ Lid Temperature Control System for Uniformity Improvement
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The lid temperature control system plays a critical role in maintaining process environment, particularly by managing thermal conditions within etch chamber. More importantly, when facing different processes and recipes, and if the chamber idle time is too long, the first-wafer effect is triggered <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. Maintaining a stable and uniform process temperature is incredibly challenging, Sym3™ lid temperature control system is fully capable of doing this. In this paper, the configuration and mechanisms will be introduced. This study explains how the entire system co-worked, interconnected to achieve the uniform and desired temperature for lid, reflected in etch rate (ER) uniformity [2].

articleTitle: Enhancing Alliance VLSI Toolchain by Mixed Gate-level Logic Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Alliance is an open-source CAD tool suite for very large scale integration (VLSI) design, offering a comprehensive set of features including VHDL compiler, simulator, logic synthesis tools, and automatic place and route (P&R) capabilities. However, the logic synthesis tool within Alliance faces limitations when handling large-scale circuits. To address this issue, we propose an approach that extends Alliance’s ability to handle large circuits and improve the results after technology mapping. Experimental results on the EPFL benchmark suite demonstrate an average improvement of 20% in delay and a 15% reduction in area compared to the original performance of Alliance.

articleTitle: Mesoporous CeO2 Particle Abrasives with High Specific Surface Area for Enhanced Chemical Mechanical Polishing Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mesoporous spheres were prepared by an effective method for application as abrasive particles in chemical mechanical polishing (CMP). It is found that slurry containing the mCeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> provided scratch-free surfaces and improved removal rate by atomic force microscopy (AFM).

articleTitle: Solution to Sidewall Roughness of High Aspect Ratio TSV Etch in Advanced Packaging
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Through silicon via (TSV) etch is a crucial process in chip manufacturing, especially in advanced packaging. TSVs are used to connect vertically stacked chips, resulting in short interconnections between chips and reduced device latency. With the increasing aspect ratio (AR) of TSV, the balance between passivation and etch is more difficult to control during the TSV etch, resulting in more sidewall roughness issues. For high aspect ratio (HAR, AR>10) TSVs, the most challenging sidewall roughness issues include Si damage, striations and the trade-off between the two. These sidewall roughness issues degrade post metal filling in TSVs and the final electrical properties of the device. In this paper, the TSV sidewall roughness mitigation approaches are studied with Lam Research’s Syndion<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> Etcher. The trade-off between Si damage and striation is broken by effective passivation management along the formation of TSV. Si damage formed at the top of the TSVs is mitigated by shorter precoat time, and lower bias voltage in RAP passivation phase. And the striation formed in the middle of the TSVs is mitigated by lower bias voltage and higher pressure in RAP passivation phase. Top damage and middle striation free HAR TSV etching is achieved in Syndion. This provides TSV benchmark solution for advanced packaging.

articleTitle: A Generic Solution to Handle System in Package Efuse Test in Multiple Flow
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Many ATE Test programs still rely on a code based Efuse Test Method, resulting in lengthy development times, extended test durations, and a higher risk of device rework. Furthermore, the presence of one-time-programmable fuses introduces the risk of critical quality issues arising from coding errors.This paper addresses the challenges of SiP devices’ fuse test procedure, data structure and programming ways on 93K SMT8. This adaptable solution minimizes coding efforts, ensures quality, and provides the best time-to-market (TTM) and test time for various customer scenarios. The effectiveness of this solution will be demonstrated through test cases used in several customers' Common Building Block (CBB), showcasing its ability to significantly reduce offline time and achieve successful online verification.

articleTitle: 22 Al Gate Change W Gate Improve for NMOS Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: According to 28HK learning, 22ULL+ introduces "W-MG" to improve the performance of NMOS devices, replacing AL-Gate(aluminum gate) with W-Gate (tungsten gate) can greatly reduce the resistance, while providing compressive stress on the gate, which can effectively improve the performance of NMOS devices.

articleTitle: Research on WIP dispatch rules base on dynamic standard whole process cycle time
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Most wafer fab in semiconductor manufacturing industry adopt order delivery mode, and cycle time is the key index to measure whether orders can be delivered on time. In order to ensure the timely delivery of products, the choice of dispatch mode is importance. In this paper, taking the punctual delivery rate as the production goal, the dynamic production cycle time target decomposition based on data drive is proposed to realize the real-time update of the standard production cycle time of the whole process stage, and based on the standard production cycle time, the dynamic priority change system is established, which gives the dynamic real-time priority for local dispatch demand, achieves the dynamic allocation of production line machine and resource, and ensures the smooth delivery of the production.

articleTitle: Overcoming Small Sample Size Challenges In Lithography Process Window Analysis Through DCGAN-Based Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Developing an efficient and accurate automated process window analysis method for the lithography process is a challenging small sample size problem due to the difficulty of acquiring sufficient training data. To address this, we propose using deep convolutional generative adversarial networks to augment and expand the lithography process window dataset. With this approach, we can train a lithography process window analysis tool with a smaller amount of original data while achieving performance metrics comparable to those obtained by training with a large amount of raw data. The experiments show that the required size of raw data for training can be reduced by approximately 92%.

articleTitle: Chiplet Dft Solutions for Cross-Die Testing Channels
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Due to the quantity limit of IO in chiplet , the reusable IO resources for DFT (Design For Test) are relatively scarce in availability, which causes a significant bottleneck in testing process for DFT. In this paper, we propose a DLS (DFT Lane Switch) structure that allows flexible and efficient reuse of IO resources. Furthermore, we suggest reusing the UCIE (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express) interconnect channels as test paths to increase the number of reusable channels across die. This solution increases the bandwidth of the test data, which help to reduce the time required for testing, then reduce the cost of testing. The channel switching scheme based on DLS is more suitable for chiplet, featured by a variety of packaging combinations.

articleTitle: Correction Model for Plate Mapping Error Based on Acceleration and Deceleration of Plate Stage
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In a Flat Panel Display lithography machine, plate mapping is completed in the uniform scanning state of the plate stage, plate alignment uses CCD alignment and is completed in the stationary state of the plate stage. To improve throughput, we propose a scheme to combine the plate mapping and plate alignment processes. The new scheme will introduce a new problem, resulting in an error in the mapping result. This paper analyzes the correlation between the acceleration and deceleration of the plate stage and plate mapping errors and presents a correction model. With the correction model, experiment shows that plate mapping error is reduced by 80%, which meets the requirements of exposure imaging quality.

articleTitle: The Novel Strategy of Pattern Gate High Loading Controlling In ILD0 CMP Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As the semiconductor device size reduced to 28nm or smaller, the high-k metal gate technology was gradually introduced into the chip manufacturing process to improve the response speed and reliability of devices. In the gate-last scheme, after metal gate chemical mechanical polishing (MG-CMP), the gate height in the short channel region is lower than that in the long channel region. The large pattern gate high loading leads to electrical anomalies eventually. In order to solve this problem, three methods based on inter-layer dielectric level zero chemical mechanical polishing (ILD0-CMP) were explored for controlling gate height loading in this paper, which are changing the polish stop layer, adjusting the selectivity of slurry and modifying the type of ILD0 oxide film. Under the controlling of ILD0-CMP, the transmission electron microscope result show gate height loading improved 57-97% and the gate height in weak device region increased 13%-47% post MG CMP process, the loop process window is enlarged.

articleTitle: Study on Wet Alkaline Chemicals Etching of Hole Dummy Polysilicon in 3d Multi-Layer Structure
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Polysilicon, utilized as a dummy material, is an essential component in the fabrication of 3D film stacked memory structures. This study investigates the removal mechanisms of dummy polysilicon using traditional alkaline chemicals, specifically Ammonia DIW Mixture (ADM) and Tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH), within high aspect ratio hole structures. The results clearly demonstrate that TMAH etching agent offers superior uniformity and stability in the removal of dummy polysilicon compared to the ADM solution.

articleTitle: A Neural Network Model for Wafer-Scale Photoresist Thickness Prediction Using Feature-Screened Process Monitoring Data
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Uniform photoresist coating is important to increase the depth of focus and reduce the overlay errors in lithography, whose controlling depends on the accurate photoresist thickness uniformity model. In this study, we devised a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) model utilizing process monitoring data collected from sensors in the coating equipment during the spin coating process to predict photoresist thickness. Furthermore, we optimized the model by implementing a feature selection process using variance thresholding. Our results demonstrate that the accuracy of the model with screened features significantly surpasses that of the model without screening.

articleTitle: A New Theory of High-K Electrode Material Versus Low-K Electrode Mterial for High-K Metal-Insulator-Metal Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the author proposes his new theory that there are two kinds of electrode materials: high-k and low-k electrode materials. For example, RuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, IrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SrRuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> normally behave as conductors but can behave as high-k dielectric when depleted of free electrons. Metals normally behave as conductors but can behave as low-k dielectric when depleted of free electrons.

articleTitle: The PMOS Silicon Recess Process Control With Evolution of Trench Morphology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the miniaturization of device structures, the implementation of source/drain germanium-silicon embedding technology in the PMOS region is commonly employed to enhance MOSFET performance by improving carrier mobility. The PMOS silicon recess process is used for dry etching to form silicon trenches. The initial morphology of the silicon trench is a trench with a sidewall angle (SWA) of approximately 80° along the Gate spacer. To reduce the etching time required for subsequent wet etching to form a sigma shaped recess, the dry etching trench morphology is modified to a bowl shape. Subsequently, to increase channel stress, the bowl-shaped trench evolved into a U-shaped trench. Theses transformations present significant challenges for dry etching process control: as the trench becomes bowl-shaped, relying solely on Halogen gas etching fails to satisfy lateral etching requirements. This study introduces a pullback step utilizing Fluorinated gas as the primary etching gas to achieve isotropic trench etching. Additionally, when etching U-shaped trenches, the removal of sharp corners proves challenging. This study addresses this issue through a high-temperature process to effectively eliminate byproducts and form the U-shaped morphology.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Optimization for FCBGA PKG RF SI
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven optimization approach using Cadence Optimality to enhance the RF performance of FCBGA packages. By refining package routing and via designs, we achieved ~4dB margin improvement in return loss and a reduction of insertion loss by ~0.8dB at high frequency. Additionally, comprehensive link cascading and process variation validations were conducted to ensure the robustness of the optimized design. The results demonstrate AI tool can help significant advancements in signal integrity, providing valuable insights for future high-frequency electronic device packaging.

articleTitle: Automatic Partition for Hybrid Stochastic-Binary-Based Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) is an emerging computing paradigm with a smaller hardware cost than conventional binary computing (BC). In this paper, we study the effects of circuit partitions that determine which parts are implemented in the SC or BC domain on several applications. We further propose an automatic partition algorithm to find the best partition meeting the accuracy and area requirements. Experimental results demonstrate the trade-off among accuracy, area, and energy using different partitions and an average of 46.53% in energy reduction of the circuits generated by the proposed partition algorithm.

articleTitle: A Self-Calibrated Digital-to-Time Converter with High-Resolution and Wide-Range Performance Using Multi-Level Tunable Delay Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Digital-to-time converter (DTC) is widely used in automatic test equipment (ATE) and electronic measurement systems. However, high-resolution and wide-range DTCs usually require a large chip area. This paper introduces a self-calibrated DTC based on multi-level tunable delay cells with high resolution, wide range, and good linearity. The design significantly reduces the chip area. The on-chip calibration circuit reduces the OCV effect, thus enabling on-chip calibration. In a 65nm process, the design achieves a linear adjustment range of 1ns using five 5-level coarse delay cells and twelve 6-level fine delay cells. The design has a resolution of 1ps, an INL range from -2.13 to 2.6LSB, and an area of 0.0022mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Density Functional Theory Study on Mechanism for Oxygen Diffusion in Silicon with Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: An atomistic mechanism is proposed that why hydrogen enhances oxygen diffusion in silicon. We combine the ab initio molecular dynamics simulation metadynamics (AIMD-MetaD) and nudged elastic band calculation to study the migration of a single O atom with H atom in silicon. The migration paths of O and H are obtained by density functional theory calculation. The barrier of minimum energy path, which is 1.87eV, is 0.7eV lower than the energy barrier of O atom in bulk silicon. This ab initio calculation elucidates how H atom moving in silicon, which explains why the wet oxidation rate is faster than dry oxidation. AIMD-MetaD allow us to accurately learn the free-energy landscape to understand the motion of atoms during wet oxidation, which has rarely been mentioned in past studies.

articleTitle: Etching Surface and Etching Dimension Control for IGZO TFT Fabrication in 3D Memory Device
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: We investigated etching processes to form transistor hole for indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) thin film transistors (TFT) in 3D memory device. A horn-shaped profile was achieved at top of the hole to avoid gate void exposure in the coming processes. Wet etching and gas etching methods were chosen to remove liner silicon oxide covering dummy poly in the hole. It was found that gas etching process resulted in smooth profile, leading to uniform IGZO thin film without metal aggregation.

articleTitle: DC and RF Characteristics of Silicon FETs on 55nm Low Power Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth study of the direct current (DC) and radio frequency (RF) characteristics of silicon field-effect transistors (FETs) fabricated on a 55nm low power platform. We investigate key performance metrics, including the cut-off frequency (Ft), maximum oscillation frequency (Fmax), minimum noise figure (NFmin), and flicker noise (1/f noise) to assess the effectiveness of these devices for high-frequency applications. Our findings indicate that optimizing device design and fabrication parameters significantly enhances both Ft and Fmax, leading to improved RF performance while maintaining low power consumption. Additionally, we explore the trade-offs involved in minimizing NF, highlighting the impact of channel dimensions and doping profiles on overall device performance. The study also examines Laterally Diffused Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (LDMOS) and inductor designs, focusing on well implant and layout optimization. These results provide valuable insights into the challenges and opportunities in the design of silicon FETs and inductors for next-generation electronic and communication systems.

articleTitle: Cleaning and Assessing Particles from Polymer Materials Used in Semiconductor Manufacutring Tool
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Ultrasonic cleaning is a mature technique to remove particles ranging from micron to sub-micron from a wafer surface. In this study, the effectiveness of an in-house cleaning procedure in removing submicron particle is investigated. The LPC results indicate that the IPA soaking increase the removal of particles and a single ultrasonic cleaning is less efficient to removal 1 μm or larger particles from polymer surface. This paper also studied the particles residue in ultrasonic water during the ultrasonic cleaning and a 1-day use, the overflowing water for 1-hour is sufficient to remove particles from PPU surface.

articleTitle: Classification and Recognition Methods for Wafer Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Based on the defect image information obtained from wafer scanning, this method compares defect features by combining the characteristics of defect images within and between different layers. This method mainly uses machine learning algorithms to extract and classify the characteristic information of defect images. Through learning and training on the features of scanned defects, and in combination with the features of training defect images, it conducts classification training and learning for defects. It compares and identifies newly added types of defect images. For small defect type images, it compares and identifies the differences between the defect images and the reference images. By applying the nine - grid defect division method, it detects and classifies tiny and subtle defects, and detects the defect difference information in the defect images. By extracting the SAM features of the online scanned defect images, it obtains the defect features of the wafer images. Based on the defect scanning classification results, it conducts a correlation analysis between the scanned defects and the product yield to locate the problematic process. This method can automatically locate the scanned defects according to the characteristic information of the scanned defects and the product yield, thereby improving the product yield.

articleTitle: Reducing Leakage Current of Mosfets by Optimizing the Grain Size of Polysilicon Gate
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The magnitude of leakage current between source and drain of metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) is a critical parameter for evaluating their performance. Generally, MOSFETs should exhibit low leakage current in off-state, which contributes to reduced power consumption and heat generation. A significant off leakage current in MOSFETs may generated due to ions inject to channel along polysilicon grain boundary in ion implant process. In this work, the polysilicon grain size of MOSFET had been optimized and the performances were fine investigated. We found that optimization can refine the grains of polysilicon gate, which effectively reduces the impact of ion implantation on channel and greatly reduced the leakage current. In summary, the modification of polysilicon grain size can give an idea to reducing leakage current in MOSFETs.

articleTitle: RNN-Based Proxy Modeling for TCAD Simulation of Trench Mosfet Manufacturing Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient recurrent neural networks (RNN) based technology computer aided design (TCAD) proxy model that accurately simulates the process of Trench metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) devices. The model significantly accelerates the simulation process while maintaining high accuracy in predicting the device's electrical performance. The verification is carried out on a N-type Trench MOSFET with a 150nm gate feature size. The model generates predictions in under 1 second, achieving an accuracy greater than 98% when compared to traditional TCAD simulation results.

articleTitle: Chamber Conditions Control with Waferless Auto Clean Strategy in BEOL Aluminum Metal Etching Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Waferless auto clean (WAC) has been used to clean the chamber after each wafer. However, unsuitable etching chemical reactions and post process WAC will change the chamber conditions to induce the etch rate drift or fall-on particle issues. In this paper, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> is proposed to replace N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in BEOL aluminum metal etch. A series of experiments are taken to enhance the insitu WAC efficiency. As a result, a stable and reliable manufacturing process can be achieve through the optimum of etch chemistry and WAC time.

articleTitle: Effects of Injection Volume and Temperature on Spin Coating Uniformity: an Openfoam Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Maintaining the uniformity of the photoresist layer during the spin coating subprocess of photolithography is crucial for subsequent processes in wafer fabrication. Poor spin coating performance can lead to photoresist waste and defects in the final chip. In this study, we employed OpenFOAM simulations to model the spin coating process on a wafer-sized substrate, focusing on the impact of key process factors—photoresist injection volume and substrate temperature—on coating uniformity. The results indicate that the injection volume of the photoresist and the substrate temperature significantly affect the morphology of the photoresist film during the spin coating process, providing valuable insights for optimizing the coating process.

articleTitle: Addressing Thermal Challenges in SOI with Silicon-on-Silicon Carbide Heterointegration
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The buried oxide (BOX) of the Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) inhibits heat dissipation from the Si film and leads to a significant self-heating effect (SHE). This article demonstrates a novel hetero-integration process and device architecture utilizing Silicon-on-Silicon Carbide (Si-on-SiC) technology to effectively address the thermal challenges in SOI. TCAD simulations of the SHE of this architecture are performed and compared with that of SOI. Under higher voltages at room temperature (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>=V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>=1.8V, 300 K), Si-on-SiC exhibits only 2.2% self-heating induced current degradation which is significantly improved compared to the 10.2% in SOI, while the maximum lattice temperature rises by 11.5 K which is also lower than the 57.9 K in SOI. Furthermore, standard high-k/metal gate CMOS process was developed for this novel substrate and both n- and p-type MOSFET devices were successfully fabricated, demonstrating that this SOI-like architecture is fully compatible with standard CMOS processes.

articleTitle: Micro Loading Improvement in Gate Etch
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Due to the different pattern densities on the wafer surface, micro loading occurs in the isolated(ISO) pattern and dense pattern areas. Specifically manifested as slower etching in dense area, etching faster in ISO area, which resulted in the etching depth loading of two areas in gate etching. And it will lead to the poly bottom profile loading for different pattern densities. Seriously, damage on the substrate Si of ISO area is already present before dense area etching to the end. This is not acceptable in Gate etching. Therefore, this paper addresses the micro loading issue within a tradition film stack structure of poly gate etching.

articleTitle: A Novel Inversion Approach for Predicting Critical Etch Dimensions Based on Electrical Parameters
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the ongoing miniaturization of semiconductor devices, the precise observation of etch profiles has become indispensable for optimizing the etching process. This paper proposes a novel method for predicting the critical dimension of etch profile based on electrical parameters. Utilizing simulated electrical parameters and critical etch profile dimensions obtained from identical etch process recipes, this study employ machine learning algorithms to establish a predictive model mapping electrical parameters to the critical dimensions of etch trenches. The model exhibits a coefficient of determination (R-squared) of 0.9841 and a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.0016, thereby validating the feasibility of this approach.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Surfactant Concentration on the Planarization Effect of Quartz Wafers
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Quartz crystal components are widely used in mobile communications and optical communications. With the rapid development of intelligent electronic products and mobile terminals, there is a pressing demand for compact quartz crystal devices that are reliable in performance and offer higher, more stable output frequencies. The surface quality of quartz crystals directly affects their frequency stability and temperature-frequency characteristics, and other physical properties. Despite ultra-precision polishing, the surface and subsurface of the quartz wafer continue to exhibit a damage layer. Chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) can precisely control the surface quality (Sq) of quartz wafers. Surfactants, as a crucial component of the polishing slurry, effectively enhance the surface smoothness and uniformity of quartz wafers. This study investigates the impact of different concentrations of isooctanol polyoxyethylene ether(JFC-E) as a surfactant on the surface quality of quartz wafers after CMP. Experimental results indicate that at a pH of 10.0, a cerium oxide (CeO2) concentration of 2 wt%,a hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) concentration of 1.2 wt%, and a JFC-E concentration of 90 ppm, the sample achieved the finest surface quality, with Sq of only 0.0862 nm. This result represents a significant improvement when compared to the initial surface quality of the simple, which was characterized by Sq of 2.3690 nm.

articleTitle: Zero-defect Solutions for Automotive Semiconductor Devices Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Automotive semiconductor devices need to cope with harsh conditions and complex tasks in the vehicle environment, so there are stringent qualification and verification standards and complex testing and monitoring requirements for device manufacturing. The goal of zero-defect is key to the efficient, reliable and high-volume production of automotive semiconductor devices. This review describes how Lam Research Corp. is providing solutions to achieve zero-defect performance in all areas (wafer frontside, edge/bevel, and backside) of the entire wafer. Frontside defects can be reduced by innovative honeycomb gas injector and Corvus® design in Kiyo® series etcher. Black Si defects at wafer bevel/edge can be inhibited by bottom shadow ring (BSR) on Syndion®, or bevel deposition or etching approaches on Coronus®. For arcing defects caused by tungsten (W) residual in edge area, DOMOER design in ALTUS® reduces W residual after CMP. Wafer backside deposition by VECTOR® DT not only compensates for wafer profile, reducing crack or peeling defects caused by wafer wrapping, but also acts as a barrier layer to suppress the doing effect from highly doped substrate to frontside epitaxial layers of power and CMOS image sensor (CIS) devices.

articleTitle: Improvement of W CMP Erosion Defect and Planarization Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Tungsten CMP (W CMP) has been broadly applied to the major process for local as well as global planarization of integrated circuits (ICs). W CMP process is drove by chemical interaction. In addition, W slurry consists of abrasive particle, dispersants, W removal rate enhancer, pH adjustor, inhibitor, oxidizer and so on. For W CMP, minimum erosion is necessary, which is closed related to oxide inhibitor to reduce oxide loss. Low over polish pressure with excellent planarization performance and low erosion defect were investigated

articleTitle: Investigation of NOR flash Floating Gate (FG) Residue defect improve
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Floating gate (FG) residue is one of the major defects of NOR Flash products, introduction of "ox loss" concept and through the past data research "ox loss" relationship with the defect, the study found that ox loss and defect fail was significantly negative correlation, and different products have different "ox loss" threshold. Fail bin and ox loss curve has the same turning point as the above methods, show that the method can get considerable credibility of ox loss data. Further, combining with the defect and CP data can determine the appropriate ox loss control value. Based on the mechanism of defect, put forward to solve the defects of process improvement direction: adjust the STI CMP or CVT WET extend the FG CMP window. Choose one of the direction to design experiment, the results show that "STI CMP OP-" can effectively improve the FG CMP window.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification on Multiscale Modeling of RRAM Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This work employs the uncertainty quantification method to systematically analyze the power consumption and forming voltage in RRAM devices, emphasizing the significant role of material factors in multiscale and multiphysics processes. The uncertainty quantification approach drives a macroscopic-scale thermoelectric model to simulate RRAM switching and identifies key parameters. Furthermore, the same approach is adopted to control a mesoscale phase-field model that simulates the kinetics of conductive filament evolution. The results of the two models complement each other and provide a better understanding of the dynamics occurring inside the RRAM device and the origin of the performance uncertainty.

articleTitle: Study on Key-factors Analysis of ELK Dielectric Stress
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: To reduce crosstalk and latency between chip interconnection lines, filling ELK dielectric materials between chip interconnection lines has become a common phenomenon in the semiconductor industry. However, ELK dielectric materials are susceptible to mechanical stress, leading to potential cracks. During the manufacturing process, a new thermalbudget will inevitably be introduced, and the new thermal budget will increase the thermal mismatch between different materials. The mismatch of CTE between the package substrate material and the chip material causes stress. The stress will gradually spread to the chip over time, causing the ELK crack. In this paper, the global-local simulation analysis is applied to investigate ELK dielectric stress during the cooling stage of reflow process. Impacts of different structures and materials on ELK dielectric stress are analyzed. The results indicate that UBM size, pre-solder materials, substrate core CTE, bump density, PI thickness, pilliar height have a significant impact on the local stress of ELK layer.

articleTitle: RF Switch-LNA Integration for RFFE In 65nm SOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Design and analysis of high performance RF Switch and LNA with technology co-optimization is integrated for RFFE with cost effective in 65nm SOI process. A high performance RF switch SPDT is design and realized with insertion loss (IL) lower than 0.4dB and isolation greater than 24dB from 0 to 8GHz bandwidth with peak power operation capacity greater than 36dBm while harmonic distortion power <-54dBm. Design of 45V antenna tuning switch SPSTx4 achieves pure IL of one SPST is less than 0.28dB while the pure isolation is greater than 11dB from 0 to 6GHz with peak power operation capacity greater than 43.5dBm while harmonic distortion lower than -48dBm. Design of a low power full integrated cascode LNA at 2.5GHz is implemented with gain of 22dB, NF of 0.7dB, P1dB and IIP3 of -19.8dBm and -2.2dBm. It demonstrates great potential of high performance low cost RF Switch-LNA integration for advanced RFFE module SoC applications in 65nm SOI technology.

articleTitle: Effect and Optimization of Ge Pre-Amorphous Implantation on Nickel Silicide
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The effect of energy and dose of Ge pre-amorphous implantation (PAI) on the quality of nickel silicide (NiSi) and the roughness of NiSi/Si interface is investigated. With the increase of PAI energy and dose, the thickness of amorphous silicon (a-Si) formed gradually increases, and the sheet resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) of NiSi also increases. With medium energy and low dose, the roughness of the NiSi/Si interface is effectively improved, and the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> is reduced by 8.96%.

articleTitle: The Structural Optimization of LDMOS with Low-Temperature-Oxide Field Plate
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This work is dedicated to enhancing the electrical performance of high-voltage LDMOS devices based on 0.18μm BCD platform. It analyzes the key components of an LDMOS with the field plate structure that influence device performance, and systematically scales them to find the optimal combination. An appropriate TCAD simulation is employed to investigate the underlying mechanisms and to inform the strategies for enhancement. Ultimately, both the breakdown voltage and specific on-resistance of the device exceed the stipulated design criteria of a standard 35V LDMOS, which are 54V and 20.61 mΩ•mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. Moreover, the figure of merit (FOM) demonstrates an improvement compared to the benchmark.

articleTitle: RRAM-Based in-Memory Computing for Intelligent Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has fueled a heightened demand for highly energy-efficient chips. Nevertheless, conventional von Neuman computation architectures encounter critical bandwidth bottlenecks when handling vast amounts of real-time data processing. In-memory computing (IMC) paradigms leveraging resistive random-access memory (RRAM) have demonstrated remarkable potential in enabling these burgeoning intelligent applications. In this paper, we have demonstrated our efforts on RRAM-based IMC systems, encompassing the design of RRAM devices and the implementation of RRAM-based IMC chips. We envision these works may set the stage for future applications in RRAM in-memory computing technology.

articleTitle: Application of Wsmx Cards in Sensor Chip Testing and The Resulting Simplification of Test Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper introduces the application of the WSMX card in the testing of automotive electronic sensor chips and the simplification of the test circuit by the flexible internal structure of the WSMX card. For general use circuit of sensor chips that use differential signals as input, single-ended signals are often used as input during testing, and then converted through a single-ended to differential circuit. However, the differential interface inside the WSMX card has Offset DACs at the P and N terminals, which can flexibly adjust the output voltage and directly transmit it to the sensor chip as a differential interface, avoiding the effects of manual and software zero calibration and temperature drift.

articleTitle: Study on Improving Local Mismatch of 0.305μm2 Small Size SRAM
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Static random access memory (SRAM) is widely used in sensing applications and in a wide variety of other ASIC and system chips. In order to obtain the maximum SRAM capacity while further reducing the chip area, SRAM usually uses the minimum size allowed by the corresponding technology node. However, when the chip size is reduced, the local mismatch between adjacent transistors of the SRAM unit is also more serious, resulting in low yield of the chip. In this paper, based on the SRAM structure with mature technology and mass production, the size is miniaturized by 20% to develop a smaller size of SRAM. Based on the process and device perspective, by optimizing the core NLDD implant and hard mask for polysilicon gate etch, the local mismatch between adjacent transistors of SRAM cells are reduced, The V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MIN</inf> (it is twenty percent lower than normal voltage) yield of SRAM test wafers are increased 130%. At the same time, the program is based on the HV mature process platform development, no additional mask, cost saving, stable and controllable, suitable for mass production.

articleTitle: Enhancing Predictive Performance and Efficiency in CMOS with Optimized CNN Hyperparameters
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Data-driven machine learning is valuable for analyzing transistor devices, but deep learning often requires large datasets and computational resources, limiting practical use. Traditional models applied to inline data tend to overfit due to high-dimensional parameters and data discontinuities. We propose a machine learning model that combines fully connected neural networks (DNN) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) to predict the parameters of 55nm 7V CMOS devices. This approach efficiently tunes hyperparameters, minimizes overfitting at lower computational cost, and achieves significant improvements in predictive performance.

articleTitle: Investigation of the GIDL Current Shift Phenomenon in Symmetrical High-Voltage NMOS Devices on 55 nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A comprehensive investigation into the Gate-Induced Drain Leakage (GIDL) current shift phenomenon observed in symmetrical high-voltage (HV) NMOS devices fabricated using advanced 55nm technology was presented in this work. Through a combination of experimental measurements, device simulations, and physical analysis, we elucidate that the factors leading to the variation in leakage current are oxide traps located at the gate poly edge. The GIDL current shift phenomenon results in an unstable leakage current of HV NMOS devices, failing to meet the required specifications. In addition, this paper presents a viable solution that can effectively reduce the variation in GIDL current. The findings provide crucial insights for optimizing device design and improving reliability in future high-voltage applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Noise Sensitivity Based Critical Path Selection
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Dynamic noise has become a critical concern in nanometer-scale digital integrated circuits (ICs), significantly affecting timing analysis and critical path identification. Traditional methods often overlook the impact of dynamic voltage fluctuations, leading to suboptimal optimization and potential timing violations. This paper proposes a dynamic noise sensitivity-based critical path selection methodology that incorporates logic gate noise sensitivity into path-level analysis. By accurately accounting for dynamic noise effects, our approach enhances the identification of critical paths most susceptible to timing issues. Experimental results on ISPD2012 benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves higher accuracy than traditional techniques with minimal computational overhead, improving the reliability and performance of large-scale digital ICs.

articleTitle: Wafer Position Recognition Technology on Electrostatic Chucks
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In semiconductor fabrication, precise wafer positioning is critical for achieving accurate doping, as even slight misalignments can result in significant performance issues during the final wafer acceptance test. Electrostatic chucks (ESCs) are widely utilized during the implantation process to securely hold wafers in place, relying on electrostatic forces to maintain stability and prevent movement. Ideally, wafers are centered on the ESCs; however, slight positional shifts may occur due to vacuum inconsistencies, transport irregularities, or notch misalignment. Recognizing and correcting wafer positioning are essential to ensuring process stability and yield. Despite its importance, no wafer positioning technology has been widely adopted in integrated circuit manufacturing. This paper introduces a wafer position recognition system designed for application on ESCs. Leveraging advanced imaging technology, the system employs a high-resolution camera to capture wafer images. By incorporating a triangular arrangement of calibration pins, a precise calibration area is established to facilitate accurate positioning. The system analyzes the gray values in four distinct zones along the wafer boundary to determine its exact position on the ESC. The proposed system effectively minimizes the risks of wafer misplacement, fall-off, or collision, thereby improving process stability, enhancing yield, and optimizing the overall efficiency of semiconductor fabrication processes.

articleTitle: A Temperature and Process Robust Logarithmic Circuit for CIM Application
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents a logarithmic interface circuit for reading current from a CIM (Computing-In-Memory) array. A BJT array is used to generate a logarithmic voltage, which is then compensated for temperature-induced variations in the output current using a cross-linear analog multiplier and a temperature-insensitive reference current generated on-chip. The proposed circuit is implemented in a standard 65 nm CMOS process and occupies an analog core area of 241 μm × 116 μm. Modules that scale with the array size require an additional 3, 000 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Post-layout simulation results show that, under a 1.2 V supply voltage and an input current from 10 μA to 100 μA, the circuit maintains less than 4% variation due to process and temperature fluctuations across a temperature range of 45°C to 95°C. Additionally, at 45°C, the circuit exhibits good dynamic performance for periodic exponential input currents with a frequency of 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Pre-Epitaxy Backside Iron Contamination Leads to Cluster Cone Defect in Shallow Trench Isolation
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Epitaxy is a key process at the front end of semiconductor manufacturing, the defect on the epitaxial film greatly affects the yield and reliability of the final product. Previous studies have focused on the impurities on the front side of the substrate silicon leading to epitaxial defects. However, in our study, the backside of the substrate silicon was contaminated with metal impurities before epitaxy, which led to an interesting clustered cone defect in the isolation trench. We carried out a series of experiments and proposed a possible hypothesis about the formation mechanism of the cluster cone defect. Furthermore, a possible solution for such a defect was also provided and verified to avoid the potential loss of yield and reliability.

articleTitle: 5G RedCap Device and its Low-Cost High Efficiency ATE Test Solution
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper explores the key differences between 5G baseline devices and 5G RedCap (Reduced Capability) devices. While 5G base line targets high-performance applications with high data rates, low latency, 5G RedCap focuses on power efficiency, reduced complexity, and moderate data rates, making it suitable for applications that don’t require the full capabilities of 5G baseline. Additionally, we demonstrate a low-cost, high-efficiency test solution for production testing on the V93000 platform, making it suitable for large-scale manufacturing of 5G RedCap devices.

articleTitle: Preparation of Nanotwinned Copper and Its Application in Advanced Packaging
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Due to its excellent electrical conductivity and mechanical strength, nanotwinned copper has significant potential applications in the field of semiconductor packaging. Nanotwinned copper with (111) preferred orientation was prepared by direct current electrodeposition and applied it in the electroplating of copper pillars and redistribution layers (RDL). These studies show that the nanotwinned copper pillars prepared by a novel additive system have excellent microscopic uniformity with total indicated runout (TIR) value less than 8%. Copper pillars with nanotwinned structures are thermally stable below 450 °C. For the application of RDL, 4 μm line with nanotwinned copper structures could be obtained with a uniformity of <5%. The above results indicate that the innovative additive system has an excellent application prospect in advanced packaging nanotwinned copper plating.

articleTitle: Inverse Lithography with Curvilinear Mask Rule Compliance
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the challenge of printing ever-shrinking features on wafer, inverse lithography techniques (ILT) has been crucial for enhancing pattern fidelity and improving process windows. However, the introduction of curve features will lead to apparently many more and undefined mask rule check (MRC) violations with traditional rectilinear-based detections. In this paper, we perform curvilinear intra-feature width and inter-feature spacing violation detection and various subsequent correction strategies with feature-skeleton based distance maps. We further incorporate mask rule check and correction into a level-set based optimization framework to prevent the recurrence of previous violations. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively resolves MRC violations while ensuring pattern fidelity.

articleTitle: Application and Mechanism Research of Novel Green Chelating Agent in CMP
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of poly-aspartic acid sodium salt as a novel green and efficient chelating agent on improving the copper removal rate and surface quality is studied. Characterization is given by measuring particle size, zeta potential, contact angle, and atomic force microscopy (AFM), as well as density functional theory (DFT).

articleTitle: Precision Analysis and Hardware Acceleration for Large-Scale Quantum Fourier Transformation on Modern FPGAS
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of quantum algorithms and practical quantum computing devices, how to efficiently simulate emerging quantum algorithms via quantum circuit simulators on classical parallel-computing hardware platforms has raised more and more interest. The superior customized parallelism and pipeline efficiency over general-purpose processors make FPGAs ideal for large scale quantum algorithms/circuits simulation. Since the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) has been used in many quantum algorithms, such as quantum linear algebra, quantum phase estimation and quantum machine leaning, this paper presented a novel precision analysis and an efficient customized-precision QFT simulator accelerated on AMD Alveo U55C FPGAs. Customized-precision representations via high-level synthesis are employed for QFT implementation with up to 16 qubits, demonstrating up-to 8.3× speedup versus implementations in floating-point arithmetic within an error tolerance of 0.1%.

articleTitle: Study on Improvement of FG Residue in NOR Flash by Etching Back
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: NOR Flash is a non-volatile semiconductor memory that can retain data for a long life when power is turned off. It is a form of electronically erasable programmed read-only memory that allows it to be erased or written multiple times during operation. erasing data of NOR flash is based on the F-N tunneling effect (Fowler-Nordheim), where electrons are tunneled through a dielectric layer to the silicon substrate, and the writing is injected into the Floating gate (FG) by hot electrons, which are released and captured to achieve 1/0 signal recognition. Therefore, FG related process is very important for NOR performance. At present, STI is the end point of FG CMP (Chemical Mechanical Polishing) process, and the general Oxide loss is 80~100 Å. However, due to insufficient filling capacity of STI loop, seams are easily generated in the center position, subsequently causing FG to be deposited in the void, and the CMP process cannot completely remove buried FG, resulting in Poly residue. Such defects will cause annular failure map, resulting in low yield. In this paper Most of the top FG poly was first removed by FG CMP, with OX loss 30~50 Å as the end point, and the poly residual was removed by the second dry etching, which overcomes the disadvantage that pure CMP process is difficult to completely grind FG residue on STI. At the same time, the thin thickness of FG caused by over-grinding can be avoided to ensure good cell performance. After improvement, the yield is improved by at least 2%

articleTitle: Optimization of Filling Capacity in Harp Process for STI Void Defect Reduction in Advanced Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: STI void, which is formed because the HARP deposition cannot effectively fill oxide and will lead to the loss of a layer of film in the subsequent process, resulting in lower yield. In this paper, STI void was exposed on the surface by adding dip oxide firstly, and then STI void can be detected by the EBI machine. HARP filling performance is optimized by reducing chemical flow rate and adjusting the offset setting of the machine. The results show that this action can successfully improve 99% of STI void defects, improving product yield.

articleTitle: Retaining Ring Wear Study with Ceria Slurry in Chemical Mechanical Planarization
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Retaining ring in CMP polisher is a consumable and could contribute significantly to overall cost of ownership. Longer retaining ring life is desirable. Thereafter, we carried out a study of retaining ring wear rate regarding to retaining ring materials and ceria slurries and abrasives. We find the type of retaining ring materials can show significant impact on the retaining ring wear rate, in which PET type of retaining ring is up to 2.5 times lower wear rate than PPS. Ceria abrasive type and size can impact retaining ring wear rate as well. Adding dispersants to ceria particles can greatly reduce retaining wear rates than bare particles.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Improvements of TSV Distortion Characteristics in High Aspect Ratio TSV Etch
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the TSV abnormal distortion characteristics of the silicon through hole in the TSV etching process are investigated. At first the origin of the abnormality in the process of TSV etching is analyzed. Then a new processing and measurement calculation method about the TSV process is developed to characterize the TSV distortion index. Moreover, a series of key parameters are summarized based on the experiment data to quantify the distortion characteristics of the TSV in the recipe. Finally, a guide of new structure design is proposed to improve the TSV distortion based on the analysis to TSV process tool.

articleTitle: The Integration of Low-K Films Into MOSFET Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The integration of low-dielectric materials in advanced semiconductor devices is critical for reducing parasitic capacitance and enhancing performance. Silicon oxycarbonitride (SiOCN) has been identified as a promising material for low dielectric constent (low-k) material gate sidewall spacers in MOSFET technology. This study examines the integration of SiOCN spacers within MOSFET gate structures. Device gate patterning was performed using electron beam lithography (EBL) and self-aligned double patterning (SADP) process, ensuring precision and scalability. SiOCN films, prepared via atomic layer deposition (ALD), exhibit excellent uniformity and demonstrate strong compatibility with anisotropic etching processes. These features make them highly suitable for advanced device applications.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency and Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Engine with Parallel – Pipeline Pooling Scheme
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper developed a very high-energy-efficiency neuromorphic chip is proposed and demonstrated with 55nm CMOS technology which is free-expandible to the suitable scales to meet the requirement of various AI applications. A novel compact even-driven near-memory MAC module is proposed based on binary spiking neural networks (BSNNs) to minimize both memory volume and memory access. Additionally, a parallel-pipeline pooling scheme is adopted using a multi-threaded post-convolutional max-pooling computation, to further reduce the data access for intermediate results during convolution processing. The prototype chip with four MAC modules was designed and fabricated under 55nm-CMOS technology for image recognition. The chip results verified a high-energy efficiency of 21.08TOPS/W @1.2V/ 100MHz with a handwritten-digit recognition accuracy of 96.92%.

articleTitle: Trench Punch Study for Two Different Material Interface
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Punch process is a method to etch high-aspect-ratio bottom layer without top damage. The structure of punch process is usually cyclic dep/etch/strip. People are more focused on pillar punch while the trench punch is rarely studied. This article studies trench punch with two different material interface, poly silicon and Silicon Nitride. It means that it is important to care not only what it is cared in pillar punch, but also the selectivity of poly and nitride. Moreover, boundary damage is studied in the article and two possible solutions are proposed.

articleTitle: Si top corner damage-free etch process for shallow trench isolation
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Shallow trench isolation in large-scale integrated circuits is currently the main isolation method. With the increase of integration density, the requirements of shallow trench isolation technology are getting higher and higher. In this paper, the problem of sidewall damage in shallow trench isolation (STI) etching is solved by adjusting the selection of process parameters. In the experiment, the formation of polymer is controlled by changing the content of O2 to solve the problem of Si top damage. After solving and optimizing the process difficulties of shallow trench isolation in this article, the performance of the obtained isolation structure fully meets the requirements of large-scale mass production of logic device technology.

articleTitle: The Etching of SiO2/Mo-MoN/SiO2/TiN Stacks in an Inductively Coupled Plasma System
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The dry etching characteristics of Silicon oxide/Mo-MoN/Silicon oxide/TiN films to form channel hole structure were investigated using an inductively coupled plasma system. In this work, silicon oxide was etched with CF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/CHF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/AR gas, TiN was etched using Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/AR gas, and Mo-MoN was etched under Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>/O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas conditions. It was found that replacing the etching gas of Mo-MoN film from Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>/O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, a relatively smooth and vertical Silicon oxide/Mo-MoN/Silicon oxide/TiN channel hole structure is obtained.

articleTitle: Array center and array corner loading effect improvement in r-SADP
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Reverse Self-aligned Double Patterning (r-SADP) process is a very important technique in trench etching of Dynamic Random Access Memory devices. In the r-SADP etching process, due to the distinct etching environments at the center and corner of the array, there are differences in the etched trench critical dimension at the center and corner, which will adversely affect the performance and yield of the device. This paper investigates the impact of pressure, source power, and gas during the carbon etch-back (C-EB) step in the r-SADP process on the loading effect observed at both the center and corner of the array. The results indicate that applying high pressure during the C-EB over etching step can effectively alleviate the loading effect at the center and corner of the array in the r-SADP process.

articleTitle: Impact of Dielectric Environment and Thickness on MoS2 CVD Growth
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In order to explore the direct growth of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on different dielectrics for scaled transistors fabrication, a theoretical and experimental investigation of the adsorption properties of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on different dielectrics are conducted. In this work, we observe that the dielectric environment and thickness both could impact MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> chemical vapor deposition (CVD). MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> shows a lower absorption energy (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>) on amorphous HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> than amorphous SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, which is also confirmed by higher nucleation densities and larger surface coverage of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> during the same CVD process. Notably, for the first time we find thinner dielectric films could prompt the lateral growth of monolayer MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, because thicker dielectric films are easier to become polycrystalline under the MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> growth temperature. This study provides a detailed study of dielectric’s impact on Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor deposition and paves the way for direct integration of 2D-semiconductors based devices on deposition substrates.

articleTitle: Analysis and Improvement of Measurement Accuracy of Insertion Loss
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of communication technology, more and more products need to measure the insertion loss, so it is more and more important to measure the loss value accurately. Occasionally, resonance, interference and jitter will occur in the measurement, which will lead to abnormal results, and the measurement value deviates from the linear law of the target at a single frequency, PCB design and measurement workers often bring serious confusion. In order to measure the design and measurement accuracy more accurately, this paper mainly aims at the difference between the long and short lines (X2-X1) in DELTA-L measurement method, the difference between Delta-L 3.0 and Delta-L 4.0, and the influence of back drilling on resonance, the accuracy of far-end and near-end via measurement, and the influence of pitch distance between lines on Set2dil measurement. It is found that Delta-L measurement with X2-X1≥5inch, increasing back drill and using Delta-L 4.0 can improve the measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: A Study of Minimum ISO-Dense Etching CD Bias Loading Performance on Advanced Logic Trench Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Iso-dense loading including critical dimension (CD), depth and profile etc. is becoming a challenge for both Logic front-end-of-line (FEoL) and back-end-of-line (BEoL) patterning due to the need to scale the pitch [1] - [2]. In this paper, trench process iso and dense CD performance had been evaluated for both devise and reliability uniformity window. By using AppliedPRO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> [3], a systemic investigation was performed to find the tuning knobs of iso to dense etching CD bias loading. Based on DOE and tuning knob window split, our results indicate that iso to dense CD bias loading can be tuned. This study demonstrates efficient way to find the tuning knob and develop relative etching recipe.

articleTitle: Time-Multiplexed Alternating Plasma Etching of Piezoelectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Piezoelectric materials, such as Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>N and PZT, are key building blocks for wave filters, which has applications in 5G communications. In this work, we demonstrate a time-multiplexed alternating process for the plasma etching of piezoelectric materials. Compared with the traditional plasma etching method, the plasma etching results, such as has uniformity, residuum, and bottom metal electrode loss/damage, can be better controlled in time-multiplexed alternating process.

articleTitle: The process of etching high aspect ratio SiB at high temperature
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Silicon boron (SiB) often plays a role of hard mask material for HAR (high aspect ratio) dielectric etching process, which has the advantage of high selectivity. In this article, we mainly studied the process of etching high aspect ratio SiB at high temperature. With a mask, this process etch through SiB and stop in underneath dielectric film, we increased the evaporation of by-products during the etching process by raising the temperature, increased the etching rate, and utilized multi frequency pulse technology to provide high selectivity and improve the LCDU; At the same time, by adjusting the bias power and gas ratio, we solved the problem of polymer accumulation on the oxide top and SiB sidewall, and obtained an almost perfect etching profile.

articleTitle: Comparison of 40MHz and 60MHz HF Frequencies in Dual-Frequency CCP for Low-K AIO Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Dual-frequency capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) etching is widely used for dielectric etching in back-end of line (BEOL) processes, such as all-in-one (AIO). In this setup, the higher frequency power primarily controls plasma density, while the lower frequency power influences ion bombardment. This study compares two common frequency combinations, 40/13MHz and 60/13MHz, analyzing etching profiles, depth, HM selectivity uniformity, and defect yield results in low-k dielectric AIO processes. Overall, with process optimization, both combinations achieve similar etching profiles. However, the 60/13MHz combination shows poorer uniformity and defect performance, which proves challenging to mitigate through hardware-based CIP adjustments.

articleTitle: Investigation on Leakage Risk of HV PNP ESD Devices in LDMOS Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
