abstract: High-voltage (HV) PNP devices are commonly designed for electrostatic damage (ESD) protection of lateral diffused metal-oxide-semiconductor (LDMOS) in automotive Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) platform. It is necessary to detect leakage failure problem of HV PNP devices in the early evaluation stage because of the leakage risk on actual application. In this paper, we used the wafer-level current limit loop-test method to measure the direct current breakdown voltage (DCBV) of the same sample several times at the limited current of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf><<I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The small current limit loop-test effectively obtained the device real DCBV while the large current limit loop-test could simulate the current state in customer real usage. It is confirmed that current limit loop-test method could screen out HV PNP ESD devices with leakage problems efficiently and effectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Line Driver for High-Speed Power Line Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this design, a differential 12-V line driver suitable for HPLC applications is proposed using TSMC 0.18um BCD process. It drives a 50 Ω load with a -40-dBc distortion with an output swing of 75% of the power supply voltage. The performance and power dissipation are comparable to the best product on the market, while consuming an active area of 1.08*1.06 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Thicker and Better Semiconductor Passivation Layers for Zero Defect Automotive Applications on 12-Inch 90-NM BCD Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The primary purpose of the passivation layer is to protect the semiconductor and is usually deposited in the final stage of semiconductor manufacturing. The performance of the passivation layer usually determines the stability of the semiconductor chip. In practice, thin passivation layers often make it difficult for chips to withstand temperature cycling tests. In the development of automotive platforms, the passivation layers need to be optimised to meet the more demanding test conditions. A series of experiments were therefore carried out on the thickness and composition of the passivation layer. The experiments proved that a thicker passivation layer could meet the higher application requirements.

articleTitle: Hydrogen-Free IBD IGZO Thin Films With Outstanding Thermal Stability And Improved Step Coverage
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Ion beam deposition technology is used to fabricate IGZO thin films with excellent thermal stability. Additionally, XPS analysis was performed on IGZO thin film to analyze the absence of hydrogen, which affects the thermal stability of the films. Furthermore, XPS depth profiling revealed homogeneous IGZO thin films deposited by the ion beam deposition. Moreover, IGZO thin films were deposited on high-aspect-ratio trenches with an aspect ratio of 6:1, exhibiting improved step coverage and conformality. The film coverage was further optimized by adjusting the angle of the ion source during the deposition process.

articleTitle: Effect of Sulfur-Containing Corrosion Inhibitors on the Selection Ratio of Removal Rate for Ruthenium Based Copper Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As integrated circuit technology develops to nodes below 10 nm, the one-step chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) process for Cu films requires a high removal rate (RR) for copper (Cu) as an interconnection material, while maintaining a near-zero RR for ruthenium (Ru) employed as a barrier. This study studied the impact of two sulfur-containing corrosion inhibitors on the RR and selectivity of Cu/Ru. The results revealed that when using 3.5 wt% L-methionine (L-Met) as a corrosion inhibitor, the selectivity ratio of Cu/Ru RR reached 310, and the surface roughness (Sq) was effectively improved.

Author Keywords: Copper Ruthenium Removal Rate Selection Ratio

articleTitle: Impact of Carrier Lining Structure on the Wafer Edge Stress in Chemical Mechanical Double-Sided Polishing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical Mechanical Double-Sided Polishing (DSP) is a crucial step in the processing of chip substrate materials. However, the wafer edge roll-off phenomenon during DSP deteriorates wafer edge flatness. By establishing a finite element model, this study investigates the impact of the carrier lining structure on the wafer edge stress during DSP. The results show that the wedge-shaped lining structure can effectively reduce stress concentration at wafer edge, thus improving wafer edge flatness. Theoretically, this study provides guidance for enhancing wafer edge flatness.

articleTitle: A Novel OPC Method Based on Pattern Density
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Traditional OPC is based on the assumption of stable lithography process with low correlation to pattern density. Normally it is accurate enough for generic IC layout. But it will depart from model prediction if the layout pattern density cannot be controlled well such as GPU/RF/CIS devices. In this paper we will demonstrate the pattern density induced OPC miss-match with traditional OPC in special IC layout. A novel OPC method with separated SSA table for different pattern density is introduced to reduce the pattern density impact and improve OPC accuracy at extreme high or low pattern density cases.

articleTitle: Charge Trapping Defects in Al2O3/SiO2/Si Structure Characterized by Spectroscopic Second-Harmonic Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Spectroscopic and time-dependent (TD) second harmonic generation (SHG) is used to study the defects states and charge trapping mechanism in an Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/native- SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si structure. Here we report an non-contact and nondestructive SHG method to investigate the electrical characteristics of the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/substrate structure. The results suggest that the time evolution of SHG is highly related to the process that electrons are excited from Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> valence band to oxygen vacancy state V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-</sup> inside Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> via resonant four-photon ionization, and then tunnels to Si substrate. SHG provides an innovative and useful wafer inspection technique to the semiconductor manufacturing industry.

articleTitle: The Method of OPC Correction for Narrow Neck Structures in LDD Layer
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Lightly doped drain (LDD) ion implantation is an important process for reducing the hot electron effect. LDD original layout is derived from other original layers through Boolean operations (EB rule). Since it is an EB rule-generated layer, it is easy to have narrow neck structures with dimensions smaller than MRC. In the model-based optical proximity correction process (MBOPC), the movement of the edges of the narrow neck structures is limited, which leads to suboptimal correction results in this region. At the same time, due to the MRC issue in this region, the mask making precision is reduced. In order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes an optical proximity correction method for these narrow neck structures. By removing a rectangular shape from the concave-corner type narrow neck structure with small width and adding a rectangular shape to the convex-corner type narrow neck structure with small space, the initial correction layer is generated before the model correction stage. After that, on the initial correction layer, edge segmentation and model iterative correction are performed to break the limitation of edge movement caused by MRC. By this method, the correction results in the narrow neck structure region are more convergent, and the distances from simulated contour to the gate channel satisfy the process requirement specifications.

articleTitle: Influence of Fluorine Implant on 3.3V NMOS Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of LDD fluorine implant on 3.3V NMOS device performance is studied. With LDD fluorine implant, reverse short channel effect (RSCE) can be reduced, which means boron transient enhanced diffusion (TED) can be mitigated. Moreover, Isub/IDS is reduced with IDS increasing, which is different from without fluorine implant. This gives more margin for 3.3V NMOS device HCI improvement. When IDS is on target, Isub/IDS can be reduced by ~26% and HCI lifetime can be improved by 4.3times with LDD fluorine implant. TCAD simulation shows less boron pileup at poly corner and lower E-field at surface with fluorine implant, which contributes to better RSCE curve and improved HCI lifetime.

articleTitle: The Effect of Post Cooling Time of Single Wafer Annealing on TDDB Reliability
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The (Back-End of Line) BEOL single wafer annealing after electroplating copper of integrated circuit manufacturing is generally used for repairing lattice damage on the surface of copper metal. This process is simple and involves a specific time of heat treatment on the wafer at a constant temperature, with minimal impact on the electrical performance of the wafer. But recent research has found that the cooling time of wafers after single wafer annealing can have a significant impact on the reliability of their devices, and in severe cases, can cause device failure. This paper investigates the impact of cooling time after annealing on device reliability and analyzes the mechanism behind it.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Multi-Core SNN Co-Processor with Subminiature Scalable Near-Memory MAC Module
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a multi-core brain-inspired co-processor based on binary spiking neural network (SNN). A multicore reconfigurable technique has been implemented and using adaptive router to realize flexible multicore interconnection and efficient parallel computing. A proximity matrix module based on binary encoding and XNOR coding is designed to reuse the matrix between data input, computation result recovery and data transfer. Thus, the 98.92 % reduction is achieved in efficiency of data computation and data transfer. The test chip for image recognition was fabricated and realized under 55nm COMS process. The results show that the chip consumes as low as 7.44 mW at 1.2 V/100 MHz with 96.92% recognition accuracy. Compared to the state-of-art works, more than 20.9% reduction in power consumption is obtained.

articleTitle: DTI Profile and Depth Uniformity Tuning by Ra and Gas Distribution
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of the semiconductor industry, dies are getting smaller and smaller and the application of DTI <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]-[5]</sup> (Deep Trench Isolation) is becoming more and more extensive. In the process of DTI demo tuning, profile and uniformity tuning have high requirements of the tool and knobs.Applied’s Sym3™Via2 conductor Etch system is equipped with an advanced RF power system, which can precisely control of plasma density for profile tuning. This paper introduces DTI profile and depth uniformity tuning by current ratio (Ra) and gas distribution Etching method.

articleTitle: Reduction of Wafer Backside Aluminum Contamination for Harp STI Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: High Aspect Ratio Process (HARP®) is widely used for shallow trench isolation (STI) gap-filling from 55nm to 28nm node. It is a high temperature process with wafer chucking function. High temperature could enhance fluorine's attack on AlN heater, and chucking force would lead to backside particles generation. This paper discussed the generation mechanism of HARP STI wafer backside aluminum contamination, and proposed two reduction methods: backside scrubbing and season film thickness optimization.

articleTitle: Picosecond Ultrasonics: An Advanced Technology Utilized for Process Control of SiCr thin Film Resistors
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process is an advanced semiconductor technology integrating Bipolar, CMOS, and DMOS devices onto a single chip, providing a compact, high-performance platform for the integration of analog, digital, and power circuitry. Thin-film resistors are employed to ensure precise resistance values and minimal temperature coefficients (TCR), thereby delivering enhanced accuracy and reliability for analog circuit applications. The SiCr thin-film resistor exhibits low TCR, consistent resistance values, minimal parasitic capacitance, and low leakage current. These characteristics surpass those of diffusion resistors, making SiCr thin-film resistor a good candidate for the precision resistance networks required in high-accuracy integrated and module circuits for BCD process. Picosecond Ultrasonics (PULSE™ Technology) has become a prevalent method in metal film measurement due to its rapid, contactless, and non-destructive capabilities. In this work, we demonstrate that Picosecond Ultrasonics has outstanding repeatability [1sigma<0.5Å] in SiCr thickness measurement as well as its excellent sensitivity to small thickness variations. SiCr thickness and uniformity could be well monitored and controlled. Furthermore, PULSE Technology can reflect the surface quality of the film by measuring the probe beam(522nm) reflectivity. Then, specialty gases flow rate would be closely monitored and controlled to achieve target SiCr thin films with desirable TCR properties.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Novel Integrated Zener Diode with Polysilicon Structure for Gate Protection in 55 nm BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: the Zener diode is a common choice for MOSFET gate protection. Compared with conventional Zener diode, a novel integrated Zener diode with polysilicon structure for gate protection in 55nm BCD technology is proposed and fabricated in this research. By optimizing the manufacture process, the Zener diode owns the stable breakdown voltage at 5.8V and leakage current at 3.62 mA. Moreover, using the polysilicon gate structure and I/O P-type lightly doped drain (IOPLDD) layer in the Zener diode can effectively avoid the Zener walkout effect caused by hot carrier accumulation around the shallow trench isolation (STI) in the conventional Zener diode.

articleTitle: Unexpected Enhancement of Aluminum Etching Rate by Increased Nitrogen Concentration in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Aluminum interconnects are critical in the production of large-scale integrated circuits, with aluminum metal etching being a key processing step. Here, we report that increasing the concentration of nitrogen—traditionally used as a protective gas during aluminum etching—enhances the etching rate unexpectedly. We have systematically investigated the effect of nitrogen concentration on the etching rate under varying pressures and etching temperatures. Furthermore, we propose two potential mechanisms to explain this phenomenon: one involving enhanced Cl₂ dissociation facilitated by excited nitrogen species, and another involving the reduction of polymeric residues through active nitrogen radicals. These findings offer key insights into optimizing aluminum etching strategies, thereby enhancing semiconductor manufacturing efficiency and quality.

articleTitle: RTPC X Pre-Thickness Control Function on Metal Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Previous thickness value is an essential parameter to qualify the wafer status in semiconductor manufacturing industry. It will significantly influence the CMP process results if the thickness is out of spec. Based on currently CMP tool, the dielectric layer thickness can be measured by optical spectrum, while metal thickness has no method to define. Here, this paper introduces a novel approach to achieve the previous thickness control function by detecting the eddy current variation for metal layer. This method greatly reduces the risk of irreversible polishing wrong product by controlling the wafer in-coming thickness for each piece of metal layer wafer.

articleTitle: Throughput Enhancement for Dual-Bit/Cell Split-Gate Floating-Gate Flash Memory Cell with Non-Self Aligned Process Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents a throughput enhancement method for split-gate floating-gate (FG) NOR-type Dual-bit/cell (NORD) flash cell. It features a common select-gate (SG) and was integrated without using triple self-aligned process, that is, with non-self-aligned process (NSA). With an additional mask and photoetch, many process steps can be removed. In the end, we can save 20% process steps in the FEOL, which decreases 10% process steps in total. The total cost had been reduced by 1.8% even though with one additional photo-mask. The performance of this NSA-cell had been studied by TCAD and characterized by experiments and finally made a mass production at our 300-mm 90-nm node technology. Additionally, a novel cell structure was proposed to improve the NSA-cell. It shows a steady and comparable performance with SA-cell.

articleTitle: A Novel DNW Isolation Structure for Reducing Device Size
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: At present, the overall supply and demand of chips is oversupply, and prices will maintain a downward trend. In order to reduce chip production costs and improve the core competitiveness of high-voltage platforms, reducing device size has become a top priority. However, the continuous reduction of the distance between DNW will lead to insufficient breakdown voltage between PN junction, and the device is easily broken down. At this time, it is very important to develop a new isolation structure to enhance the breakdown voltage. In this paper, based on the high pressure process with mature technology and mass production, the distance between DNW is reduced by 60%, and four kinds of DNW isolation structures are designed and combined with different ion implantation concentrations for the study of new DNW isolation structures. By adjusting the ion implantation concentration of PN junction and the drift region length of MOS tube, the influence of them on the breakdown voltage was investigated, and the method of increasing the breakdown voltage of MOS tube was explained. By reducing the concentration of N-type well, the breakdown voltage can reach up to 45V, which fully meets the design requirements of the device.

articleTitle: Vertical and Horizontal Profile Control in STI Etch
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: STI (Shallow trench isolation) Etch is a well-known method and widely used for active area isolation in FEOL [1] - [4]. The STI isolates each transistor from its adjacent transistor to prevent current leakage. Traditionally, this isolation is achieved through a LOCOS (localized oxidation of silicon) field oxide process. STI takes up less space while performing the same function as LOCOS, which in turn increases transistor density on the chip. CD and depth loading controlled by STI will become increasingly important to preserve the CD space, especially as the line and pitch size go down. This paper introduces shallow trench isolation method. Although there are various kinds of pattern and loading effect, the vertical profile is well controlled, and the elimination of depth loading effect are achieved, perfectly meeting the specification requirements.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm as a Design Tool for Freeform MEMS Device
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative design approach that employs a genetic algorithm (GA) in conjunction with freeform geometries for microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) at both the device and system levels. At the device level, an optimization process is performed solely within the mechanical domain. An accelerometer incorporating a freeform mechanical motion amplifier has been developed to showcase the efficacy of the proposed design methodology. Experimental findings indicate a 100% enhancement in the figure of merit (calculated as the product of sensitivity and bandwidth frequency) and a 141% increase in sensitivity when compared to a conventionally designed device. Subsequently, a system level electro-mechanical co-optimization is carried out in the electrical and mechanical domain. A closed-loop accelerometer, also incorporating a freeform mechanical motion amplifier, has been developed to illustrate the performance of the design method. The optimization procedure results in a 195% enhancement of the primary figure of merit (FOM). Measurements indicate that, in the closed-loop system, the accelerometer's displacement is reduced by 86% when a feedback voltage of 4.85 V is applied for 1 g acceleration at 100 Hz, in contrast to the open-loop system.

articleTitle: Zero Delay Cell Technology for Timing Optimization and Analysis in 3DIC Design
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative technology, Zero Delay Cell (ZDC), for timing analysis and optimization in 3DIC designs. The technology supplies an effective solution to solve the challenging problem of timing analysis optimization in 3DIC design. This paper defines a ZDC which achieves zero-delay transmission of signals, but no logical functionality. In the timing analysis, the zero-delay standard cell is used to build the timing circuit relationship between the top and bottom dies. When a signal is transmitted from one chip to another, its change can be immediate reflected at the corresponding zero-delay standard cell in the other chip, thereby completing the whole chip data transmission process without delay. Experimental results proved this technology can solve the timing optimization issues in 3DIC design. The method had been confirmed on real 3DIC design projects, proved its value in practical applications.

articleTitle: LC-VCO with Wide Tuning Range Based on 65NM Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A low-noise, wide-bandwidth NMOS cross-coupled LC-VCO is designed in a 65nm CMOS process. The oscillator select High-Q differential inductors and capacitors for thermal noise optimization and a bias current mirror as the tail current source. A configurable capacitor array extends the tuning range while maintaining low power consumption. A buffer circuit enhances output drive capability. Simulated in Cadence, the VCO achieves a frequency range of 6.64 – 10.17 GHz with a 0 – 2.5 V control voltage, phase noise of -52.19 to -64.37 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset, and a tuning gain KVCO of 31–120 MHz/V.

articleTitle: Dry Etching of Reduced Thermal Budget Borophosphosilicate Glass (BPSG) Using Furnace Anneal the Effect of Phosphorus and Boron Concentration
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The effect of phosphorus (P) and boron (B) concentration on dry etching of reduced thermal budget borophosphosilicate glass (BPSG) using furnace anneal was investigated. The BPSG film with different THK and P/B concentration was divided into three kinds type that named by top, middle and bottom, respectively. Moreover, the BPSG film was prepared by sub-Atmospheric chemical vapor deposition (SACVD) and was deposited on bare Si surface. The P and B concentration in film was checked by X-ray Fluorescence Spectrometer (XRF). Post BPSG film stabled more than 2h, rapid thermal processing (RTP) combined with furnace anneal with different anneal temperature (400°C,500°C,600°C) was designed to reduce thermal budget. Finally, the dry etch rate was performed using plasma etching. The correlation between anneal temperature, P and B concentration, as well as dry etch rate was investigated and discussed in this paper. Furnace annealing is one of the major challenges for 3D DRAM architectures, owing to the fact that the overall thermal budget on the one hand increase the diffuse range lead to the die area increase, on the other hand high thermal budget may cause lattice damage. The results of this paper indicate that the dry etch rate of BPSG film increased with increasing B concentration or B/P ratio, while decreased with increasing P concentration or P+B concentration. Nevertheless, the relationship between dry etch rate and furnace temperature is nonlinear. Thus, the dry etch rate of BPSG film can be tunning by adjusting the B or P concentration in film that suffered low temperature anneal. The results also imply that the dry etch rate of BPSG film under 400°C anneal can match with sample under 600°C anneal by slightly adjust B and P concentration. For top film, the B concentration reduce about 0.65% and the P concentration need increase about 2.61%, while the etch rate of middle and bottom film under 400°C anneal well match with samples under 600°C, thus the B and P concentration no need adjust. This investigation proved that the anneal temperature of BPSG film can reduce from 600°C to 400°C, which significantly decreased the overall thermal budget. This finding plays significant influence on the development of 3D DRAM architectures.

articleTitle: A Novel 8T TFET-MOSFET Hybrid SRAM Cell for Ultra-Low Power and Computing In-Memory Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, a novel 8T Tunnel FET (TFET)-MOSFET hybrid SRAM design with awareness of the impacts of large gate-drain capacitance in TFET is proposed and simulated. The proposed design utilizes MOSFET and TFET as upper and down transistor respectively in the read path, which can avoid the voltage coupling in conventional cascade TFET structure. Compared with conventional 6T CMOS SRAM, it achieves significant reduction in static and operation power, as well as improved static noise margin (SNM), leading to the lowest read power-delay-product (PDP). Moreover, its application for multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations in analog computing in-memory (CIM) is also demonstrated with high energy efficiency showing its great potential for energy-efficient AIoT applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Figure-of-Merit in Drain-Extended MOS with a Salicide Block Structure
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance optimization of Drain-Extended MOS (DEMOS) with a Salicide Block (SAB) structure, focusing on improving the breakdown voltage (BV) and specific on-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON,SP</inf>) to maximize the figure-of-merit (FOM) for power management applications. The study combines silicon data with TCAD simulation to analyze key structural parameters, including poly length, field plate length, slot contact length, and Ndrift-poly overlap length. Experimental results show that optimal performance is achieved by balancing these parameters, with a maximum FOM of 44.38 kW•mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The findings highlight the trade-offs between breakdown voltage and specific on-resistance, offering valuable insights for designing high-power, low-loss power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Tungsten Plug ETCH Process in IGBT Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The most common method of forming tungsten (W) plug is to etchback (EB) a blanket layer of W film and leave only the plugs intact. Two major challenges are high selectivity to the underneath barrier layer, and W residue free on a step height of topography. This paper designed W plug EB process with high etch selectivity and endpoint control model in IGBT manufacturing. Especially, thick tungsten layer can be rapidly removed by SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>/CF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> chemistry with high etch rate at the beginning of the process. The applicable O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas ratio can increase etch selectivity of tungsten to titanium nitride (W/TiN), and we precisely trigger etch endpoint by optical emission spectrometer (OES) to avoid damage titanium nitride layer at over etch step. Finally, the results show that the metal residues localized stair high spacer had been completely removed, and TiN etch stop layer had no damage. Besides, we also achieved depth controllability of tungsten recess in contact holes.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Uniformity of the Contact Resistance (Rc) of the via by the Collocation of Gas Parameters in AIO Etching
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: All-In-One (AIO) etching is commonly employed to define smaller-scale through-holes and trenches in advanced CMOS technology nodes with Cu/low-K interconnects. During the etching process, the collocation of various parameters in the recipe will have a certain effect on the uniformity of the via contact resistance (Rc) and Rc after profile , via/trench CD and final molding, among which the average value and uniformity of the via contact resistance (Rc) are particularly important. In this paper, we found that the addition of H2 to the via etch characterizes the reduction of polymer in the signal of the PR removal step CN, and has a significant improvement in the mean and uniformity of the via contact resistance (Rc).

articleTitle: Study of Metal Film Thickness on Endpoint Detection in Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP)
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In chemical mechanical polishing (CMP), it is crucial to recognize that deficiencies in the polishing process can lead to insulation between circuits that cannot be eliminated, while excessive polishing may diminish the cross-sectional area of the wiring, thereby elevating the resistance value. The endpoint detection (EPD) system is employed to ascertain the thickness distribution of the metal film and to identify the optimal endpoint necessary for achieving global flatness, thereby preventing both under-polishing and over-polishing. However, when the metal film thickness of the High Down Force (HDF) is either excessively large or small, it becomes challenging to accurately identify the inflection point on the endpoint detection curve, which adversely affects sensitivity and accuracy. This paper theoretically and experimentally analyzes the impact of HDF metal film thickness on EPD detection accuracy, and optimizes the EPD parameters and detection window. The experimental results demonstrate that the optimized EPD curve is smoother and that the success rate of capturing the endpoint has significantly improved.

articleTitle: Sram Device Threshold Voltage Mismatch Investigation and Improvement
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we have found the correlation between SRAM VtMM (threshold voltage mismatch) and key structure parameter include gate CD and NWFM THK (n work function metal thickness). In addition, we found SRAM VtMM have obvious improvement based on thick bottom TiN and shallow source/drain implant process. We separate DIBL (drain induced barrier lowing) and random doping effect on VtMM and find VtMM have strong correlation with DIBL.

articleTitle: Study on the Relationship between Transmittance and Polish Time
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As the semiconductor devices of integrated circuits achieve higher levels of integration, the increasingly significant planarization impact of transmission ratio (TR) on chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is becoming more pronounced. Different transmission ratio products may lead to abnormal Endpoint curves when used with Endpoint system, including instances like unstable Endpoint signals and timeouts. This paper presents a technique for ensuring the secure grasping of Endpoint by achieve stability in the platen 2 remove amount through modifying platen 1 polish time, additionally, a database was established to record the connections between transmission ratio and platen 1 polish time. The study demonstrates that the stability of the Endpoint curve can be achieved by regulating platen 1 polish time through the database, which is based on different transmission ratio.

articleTitle: Accelerated Simulation of Electromigration Based on Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Electromigration (EM) is a critical reliability issue in modern VLSI design. Traditional EM models often struggle with the trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. To address this, we propose an accelerated simulation approach using finite difference methods (FDM) to transform the EM system into a lumped-element circuit model. This model is further optimized with model order reduction (MOR) techniques, enabling faster and accurate stress evolution analysis. Our approach accommodates non-uniform stress distributions and time-varying current conditions. Experimental results show that our method achieves high accuracy compared to finite element analysis, providing a scalable solution for transient EM analysis in large-scale interconnects.

articleTitle: Real-Time Scheduling for Multi-Cluster Tools with Milti-Type Wafers by Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Multi-cluster tools are extensively utilized in semiconductor manufacturing. As these tools integrate more functionalities and handle increasingly complex processing recipes under numerous constraints, cyclic scheduling strategies become impractical. This paper focuses on the non-cyclic scheduling problem of multi-cluster tools with multi-type wafers and residency time constraints. A generic model is developed to describe dual-armed multi-cluster tools and propose an optimization scheduling algorithm based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enables rapid scheduling, achieving scheduling performance close to optimal and minimizing residency time.

articleTitle: Photosensitive Polyimide for Panel-Level RDL Insulator
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Processing a re-distribution layer (RDL) in a large panel, explosion-proofing processes are necessary for safety. For this reason, photosensitive insulating materials that can be developed with alkaline water and nonexplosive patterning processes are required. In addition, when using large panel, warpage due to thermal stress can also be an issue. We have developed relatively low stress fine pattern capable positive photosensitive type materials that can be developed with alkaline water, and negative photosensitive type materials that have low stress and are capable of high aspect ratio pattern processing. Furthermore, these materials have sufficient insulating reliability, and the negative-type materials can also be made into B-stage sheets. We report on these properties.

articleTitle: A DFT Test Power Consumption Optimization Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the rapid development of the modern integrated circuit process and the increasing scale and integration of chips, the test power consumption becomes a key challenge in the chip design and manufacturing process.If the test power consumption is too high, a series of problems may occur, such as increasing the load on the test equipment, affecting the reliability and stability of the chip, and reducing the yield of the chip.The introduction of clock gating has proved to be an effective technology for effectively reducing dynamic power consumption. This paper proposes a DFT test power consumption optimization scheme based on code combination logic to control ICGs, which provides an innovative circuit design idea for DFT to effectively implement low-power tests.

articleTitle: LWR Improvement in the Advanced Process Node Involved in 193nm Photoresist Treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The line width roughness (LWR) in the advanced process node is one of the most critical parameters in obtaining high yield of devices. Ar and HBr plasma treatments are widely used in curing ArF photoresist (also known as 193nm PR) before etch. The VUV light irradiation emitted by Ar / HBr plasma is known as a major role by rearranging the polymer chains and changing carbon speciation at surface to improve LWR. In this study, the effects of curing time, temperature and sequence of Ar cure and HBr cure on LWR were explored. The "sweet point" of LWR was found with increasing the curing temperature under appropriate curing time. Finally, the optimized curing process, which was applied to the fabrication of product wafer of line patterns, was demonstrated that LWR was improved.

articleTitle: Verification of PCIe over Electronic and Photonic I/Fs
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: High-speed computing (HPC) in data centers and for AI/ML computation relies largely on the high bandwidth and low latency of the interconnects between CPU, GPU, memory and storage. The high-speed serial computer expansion bus standard, peripheral component interconnect express (PCIe) 1.0 has been implemented since 2003 in CPUs and SoCs, including chip-to-chip through electronic interface (I/F) such as SerDes. Started at 2.5 GT/s, PCIe has been applied, from electronic I/F, over optic fiber or optics module. As released in 2022, PCIe 6.0 has become the latest standard to be studied over the photonic I/F. Meanwhile, the compute express link (CXL) was developed in 2019, we have initiated some study, 1) Using Alveo U50 FPGA platform for system verification of PCIe 4.0 supporting CCIX (now part of CXL) over electronic I/Fs; 2) Using Agilex 7 FPGA on high-speed Ethernet 400GbE data-rate through CMOS I/F SerDes; and 3) Based on I/F SerDes to fiber (E2O), and/or optic I/F to loopback to SerDes (O2E), the work was continued on CPO I/F. Current study aims at PCIe 5.0, at 32 GT/s or maximum 128 GB/s, over the Root Complex (host side) and the component side (endpoint side through on-board optic (OBO), to determine the system performance. The setup program for the electronic and photonic interconnect, system verification and results are presented.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Congestion-Aware Analytic Initial Routing Flow for VLSI Designs
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Initial routing is one critical step of global routing at the early stage. A recent work forms initial routing as differentiable models and achieves better routing quality by deploying it on GPUs for efficient parallel optimization. However, it still lacks enough considerations on congestion without fine-grained global layout conditions. In this work, we propose a dynamic congestion-aware analytic initial routing flow, where methods are proposed to iteratively prune nets, generate congestion-aware tree candidates, and perform tree updating. The congestion estimation becomes more precise through this procedure to provide a better solution. According to the experiments on ISPD’24 contest and ICCAD’19 contest benchmarks, the proposed flow can achieve 16.8% and 46.5% less overflow on average after global routing, compared with two state-of-the-art global routers.

articleTitle: An 80 V P-Type Organic Semiconductor-Based Power Field-Effect Transistor Featuring a Stair Gate Dielectric Structure
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In recent years, power devices are widely studied for power transmission systems, but research on organic semiconductor-based devices, hindering their potential in power applications. In this work, we present a novel approach involving p-type high-voltage (HV) organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) that utilize a stair gate dielectric (SGD) structure on both the source and drain sides. This SGD structure has successfully increased the breakdown voltage from 19 V to 80 V by effectively reducing the electric field between the drain and gate. For devices with a stair length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SGD</inf>) of 50 μm, the on-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>) shows only a 20% degradation compared to conventional devices. The proposed SGD OFETs demonstrate the capability to achieve both high breakdown voltage and low on-resistance simultaneously.

articleTitle: An Optimized and General Class-D Audio Amplifier Crosstalk Measurement Test Solution on ADVANTEST V93K ATE Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The high-power and high-resolution class-D amplifier offering a cost-effective digital input solution with low power dissipation and sound enrichment which has been popular for many years. Normally, it can be covered by ATE resources during massive production for the typical tests like high audio performance tests, FET Rdson tests, voltage, and current protection tests, snr, crosstalk, gain error. In this paper, an optimized and general test solution on crosstalk measurement of class-D audio amplifier based on hardware LC, RC filter considerations and methodology optimization has been proposed to realize the feasibility of low cost on ATE platform.

articleTitle: The Influence of Mandrel Materials in Self-Aligned Multiple Patterning Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Due to limitations in lithography resources, the application of immersion lithography in advanced nodes has reached a bottleneck. The Self-Aligned Double Patterning (SADP) and Self-Aligned Quadruple Patterning (SAQP) processes within Double Patterning Technology (DPT) not only ensure precise overlay accuracy but also effectively reduce pitch, making them essential in the production of high-end process chips. However, different devices have varying material requirements and technical standards for SADP or SAQP. Thus, the impact of the SADP film layer structure design—particularly material selection—on the final process outcomes has received increasing attention. This paper compares the effects of poly and carbon mandrels on SADP pattern transfer, focusing on mandrel material formation, key step profiles, and line roughness. It also discusses how process optimization and material selection can further enhance SADP performance.

articleTitle: Circuit Model and Wordline Driver Targeting for Wordline Open Effect in 3D DRAM
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: From the reported 3D 1T1C DRAM memory architecture, WL to WL coupling is supposed to be very high especially when vertical pitch is shrunk continuously. Under this circumstance, the effect of WL open on array operation is investigated. The worst scenario of the array pattern is that the floating cell stores "0" under open WL and processing read "1" from its adjacent normal WL, which will induce read data error. A new sub-word line driver scheme is also proposed. In the pre-simulation, the WL coupling effect could be prohibited and the current read data is obtained finally.

articleTitle: Study of the Influence of Surface Cleaning Process on SiGe Epitaxy Particle Defects
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Selective SiGe epitaxy was widely used as source/drain process to enhance hole mobility and PMOS device performance. However, the surface treatment of Si substrate is very important before SiGe film growth. Insufficient surface cleaning can cause abnormal growth of SiGe epitaxy films. Tiny particle defects are one of the most common issues in selective epitaxy process and usually caused by the low selectivity process parameters. However, surface cleaning before SiGe deposition can also result in particles and these defects can bring serious yield loss. In this paper, we studied the influence of wet cleaning process on SiGe tiny particles and the optimal surface treatment method for SiGe growth was provided.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication, and Process Optimization of Low-Voltage Super Junction TG MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel low-voltage Super Junction Trench Gate MOSFET (SJ TG MOSFET) device developed from a commercial TG MOSFET product in the 12-inch technology. This SJ TG MOSFET was investigated by TCAD simulation and characterized by experiments. A novel cost-effective method was employed to form a P-type pillar (PPL) in this work, which features multiple boron implantations. It was experimentally shown that both V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf> of 102.23 V and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sp</inf> of 49.41 mΩ•mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> were achieved in this low-voltage SJ TG MOSFET device. It was distinctly demonstrated that this SJ TG MOSFET was a competitive device in some low-voltage applications.

articleTitle: Study on Process Adjustments and APC for Precise Thickness Control of Embedded Semi-Floating Gates
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The embedded semi-floating gate (SFG) process differs from conventional logic circuits by introducing the floating gate. In the development of a process compatible with both semi-floating gate and logic regions, the formation of the floating gate can lead to significant step height and pattern loading in the logic area. This issue prevents the floating gate from being monitored through the logic pad. This paper addressed this by adjusting the U-trench hard mask deposition and etch-back process to prevent the merging of semi-floating gates between hard masks, ensuring consistent thickness of the semi-floating gate on both Active Area(AA) and Shallow Trench Isolation(STI). Subsequently, by establishing inline measurement correlation and utilizing advanced process control (APC) technology, precise control of the semi-floating gate etching thickness had been achieved.

articleTitle: Enhancing Process Stability of AIN Thin Films through Pre-Deposition in Chamber and Optical Emission Spectroscopy Assisted by Big Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In order to improve the quality of aluminum nitride (AlN) films, this study used 13.56 MHz radio frequency reactive sputtering technology through pre-sputtering chamber and used optical emission spectroscopy (OES) to measure elemental composition of gases to ensure the stability of the gas environment in the chamber [1]. Our focus is on evaluating differences in film properties such as crystallinity, surface morphology, and thickness uniformity. Our results show that the film quality of AlN is stable after the predetermined time exceeds 40 minutes, showing better crystalline quality, as evidenced by sharper and more intense XRD peaks (especially the <002> peak). Furthermore, AFM measurements show that the surface roughness of films deposited by RF sputtering decreases with increasing nitrogen concentration, with root mean square (RMS) values ranging from 1.54 nm to 3.24 nm. OES has been used to study the production of active species in plasmas excited by pulsed DC and RF power sources in nitrogen atmospheres. The higher spectral intensity observed in RF sputtering, especially the emission characteristics of ionized nitrogen (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) near 390.93 nm [2], indicates that RF plasma provides energy conditions favorable for the formation of high-quality AlN films. Furthermore, we apply principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm for big data analysis to reduce the dimensionality and visualize the clustering results of OES data recorded during different pre-deposition times.

articleTitle: A Temperature Compensating Dynamic Biasing Circuit for a K-Band Driving Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A temperature compensating dynamic biasing circuit (TC-DBC) for a K-band driving amplifier (DA) is proposed in this paper. The overdrive voltage with the positive temperature coefficient (TC) of an n-channel MOS field-effect transistor (MOSFET) and resistors with different TCs are used in the biasing circuit of the DA to compensate the transconductance variation of the amplifying transistor with temperature. In 65-nm CMOS technology, a TC-DBC is realized and integrated in a K-band DA. Experimental results show that, with the TC-DBC, from ─40°C to 130°C the transconductance variation of the amplifying transistor can be compensated, and the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> variation of the DA can be improved by 25% across the band of 17─21 GHz.

articleTitle: Silicon Trench Morphology Optimization Using ICP Etching
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In order to meet the requirements of sidewall angle and depth loading in deep silicon etching, we have studied and optimized ICP etching parameters. This study has shown that under constant etch step and bombardment step conditions, a passivation time of 15s can result in a continuous and smooth sidewall morphology. Reducing the time leads to severe lateral etching, while increasing the time will result in a trapezoidal morphology. The depth loading in pulse mode is smaller than that in CW mode.

articleTitle: A Novel Two-Stage Method for Deploying AI Models on RRAM-Based Compute-In-Memory System
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Deploying various neural network models on CIM systems automatically is a critical part of promoting the development of CIM systems. It still remains challenges to find the optimal deployment for various algorithms on CIM systems within reasonable time. Here, we propose a novel two-stage deploying method, which combines model-guided and simulation-guided deployment methods. The method can find the optimal deployment within an acceptable optimization time. The experimental results suggested that compared to the pure analytical model-guided method, the two-stage deployment method could reduce the inference latency by 28.05%, and 72.18% for ResNet-18, and Vgg-11 respectively. Compared to the pure simulation-guided method, the optimization time could be reduced by 67.69%, and 68.84% for ResNet-18, and Vgg-11 respectively.

articleTitle: Hop-CIM: An All-Digital Two-level Approximate SRAM-CIM Macro for High Energy-Efficient HNN Acceleration with Data-Aware Early Exit Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Hopfield Neural Networks (HNNs) have demonstrated effectiveness in image restoration. However, due to the intrinsically error tolerance arising from the state update criterion, performing the full precision Vector-Matrix Multiplication (VMM) to update the HNNs’ states results in computational redundancy. To address this challenge, Hop-CIM, an all-digital, two-level approximate SRAM-CIM macro is proposed in this paper with a data-aware early exit mechanism to achieve higher energy efficiency. Experimental results show that under the 28nm technology node, the proposed Hop-CIM demonstrates minimal corruption when performing image restoration on 28×28 images, as compared to the ground truths. Meanwhile, it achieves an overall energy efficiency of 941 TOPS/W, with an improvement of 1.47x and 4.44x over the traditional approximate and full precision all-digital SRAM-CIM based designs, respectively.

articleTitle: Film Etching Technique Using Halogen Plasma Following Diluted Hydro Fluorine Solution
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide (IGZO) is a leading candidate for channel material of 3D semiconductor structure due to its high mobility, high stability and low temperature processes. We developed a selectivity etching of IGZO to SiO2 using halogen based chemistry in an inductively coupled plasma (ICP) system. The actual distribution analysis of etch byproducts was performed by energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping. After plasma etch, diluted hydro fluorine (DHF) solution was implemented to clear the etch byproducts from the semiconductor topography.

articleTitle: ALE Like Post-ETCH SiC Surface Treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of society, the advancement of ultra-efficient power conversion semiconductor devices has become a key focus in the field of electronics. As a promising third-generation semiconductor material, silicon carbide (SiC) has found widespread application in various electricity-related fields, including photovoltaics, energy storage, electric charging, and electric vehicles. SiC's excellent properties, such as a wide bandgap (3.2 eV), high thermal conductivity (200 W/mK), high breakdown voltage (10 MV/cm), high hardness (Mohs scale ~9.0), and high radiation resistance, make it an ideal material for those applications<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]-[2]</sup>. During the fabrication of SiC power devices, rapid etching processes, while necessary, can introduce plasma damage that adversely affects the electrical performance and lifespan of the devices. To address this issue, atomic layer etching (ALE) technology is introduced as a post-etch surface treatment. ALE significantly reduces the plasma-induced etch damage, enabling precise etching of SiC at a highly repeatable rate of approximately 5 Å per cycle. This work provides valuable guidance for the preparation of SiC power devices in order to enhance their overall performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Investigating and Mitigating Gold Wire Stitch Breakage Failures in Tire Pressure Monitoring Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Tire Pressure Monitoring Sensor (TPMS) is subjected to a protective gel coating process on the pressure sensor, accelerometer and Microcontroller Unit (MCU) die to safeguard against environmental factors. These factors include moisture, humidity and foreign materials that could potentially cause corrosion or reliability issues. In particular, an additional gel layer is applied to the pressure sensor’s surface, followed by a subsequent coating on all three dies. During the qualification phase, the removal of the extra gel layer resulted in a failure after 1300 Temperature Cycling (TC) cycles. This failure was attributed to broken stitch wire bonding between the pressure sensor and the MCU dies. Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) analysis of the qualification samples, in comparison to a baseline pinpointed the capillary dimensions as the primary factor responsible for the failure. Simulations and empirical matching processes revealed a critical dimension that impacts bonding, leading to the broken stitch wire. Furthermore, wire bond testing highlighted suboptimal settings as a secondary contributing factor. By integrating findings from the defective capillary and the suboptimal wire bond settings, the team was able to replicate the broken stitch wire failure. Corrective measures implemented during the qualification rebuild not only allowed the device to endure 1300 cycles of TC but also to pass additional reliability tests

articleTitle: Novel IPA Filtration Technology for Advanced Wet Clean
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: It is well established that the cleanliness of isopropyl alcohol(IPA) significantly impacts wafer defects and yield. Traditionally, filters with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) membranes have been used for IPA filtration, owing to the high cleanliness performance of PTFE. This study introduces a novel polyimide(PI) membrane filter for point-of-use(POU) IPA filtration. The proposed PI membrane features a much tighter pore size distribution, a tortuous flow path, and enhanced particle capture capabilities, particularly for fine particles. Additionally, the PI membrane demonstrates strong adsorption properties for certain organic contaminants, further improving the overall filtration efficiency.

articleTitle: V-Shaped Dislocation Prevention by Selective SiGe Epitaxy Process Tuning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Dislocation is an important factor affecting the stress of SiGe epitaxial films. Besides being related to the surface treatment of the previous process, the parameter control of the epitaxial process is crucial for dislocations. Currently, V-shaped dislocation defects have appeared in the 28nm PMOS embedded source drain SiGe epitaxial films. Unlike other dislocations, this type of dislocation can cause sunken phenomenon in high germanium concentration film and having a risk of device failure. This article studies the causes and solutions of dislocations from the perspective of process recipe design.

articleTitle: Improvement of Optical Critical Dimension Metrology Accuracy Through Data Denoising
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the AA (Active Area) dry etching process at the 28 nm node, the accuracy of the OCD measurement model is significantly constrained by the uncertainty of TEM slice data. Experimental data indicate that the range of three TEM slice depths at the Center-Middle-Edge points within the same STI measurement mark reaches 12.6%, highlighting the risk of model bias stemming from anomalous TEM data in the traditional modeling process. If such data noise is not effectively mitigated, it will directly increase the OCD prediction error for trench depth and critical dimensions (CD), jeopardizing the reliability of process monitoring. This study proposes a dualthreshold collaborative optimization strategy for the OCD modeling stage: employing Cook's distance $\left( {{D_i} > \frac{4}{n}} \right)$ to identify influential TEM data and combining standardized residuals (|r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>|>2) to filter out outliers, thereby enhancing the model's generalization capability. Based on the 28 nm process dataset, the OCD prediction RMSE of trench depth and CD in the optimized model is reduced to 21.3%, and the sensitivity to TEM fluctuations within the same measurement mark is decreased by 34%. To facilitate the rapid implementation of this method by measurement personnel, an open-source Python analysis tool has been developed, which can automatically perform outlier diagnosis, model iterative optimization, and visualization report generation, significantly streamlining the process of constructing high-precision OCD models for AA etching process control.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Test Platform for 56-Gbps NRZ Digital ICs and Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This presentation briefly reviews the development of high-speed digital Automated Test Equipment (ATE) that exhibits an exponential performance growth trend which has persisted through several decades. Recent work is presented that leverages 14-28-Gbps FPGAs to extend usable test rates to 56 Gbps. This work leads to a planned development for extending beyond 100 Gbps.

articleTitle: Effects of Geometry and Surface Flatness on Direct Wafer Bonding by Multiphysics Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of wafer geometry, surface patterning and flatness deviations on bonding performance through finite element simulations using COMSOL Multiphysics. Key findings reveal that wafer geometry and waviness delay bonding wave propagation, while etched cavity enhance bonding speed. These results highlight the critical role of wafer geometry and surface morphology in determining bonding efficiency and provide valuable insight into optimizing wafer bonding processes in 3D IC manufacturing.

articleTitle: Application and Improvement of CU CMP Thickness Control Method Based on R2R System
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the back-end-of-line (BEOL) chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) process, the copper wire barrier material (Ta/TaN) and the underlying low dielectric (Low-K) material exhibit limited optical, physical, or chemical properties, which results in low-contrast signal. Consequently, reliable endpoint detection for barrier polishing poses significant challenges, leading to the common practice of employing fixed-time polishing. Due to non-ideal factors such as machine conditions and the lifespan of consumables, the amount of polishing is frequently either excessive or insufficient, leading to product film thickness that exceeds specifications and negatively impacting yield. This paper introduces a self-feedback run-to-run (R2R) system designed to automatically control polishing time on a wafer-to-wafer manner, facilitating the automatic regulation of copper wire thickness, stabilizing resistance, and enhancing product yield. Furthermore, an optimization method for the R2R system algorithm is proposed to improve feedback response time and minimize errors in copper thickness control.

articleTitle: Optimizing Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Process Metrics and Aberrations in the Cut Layer Through Source Mask Co-Optimization(SMO)
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Source-Mask Co-Optimization (SMO) techniques have significantly supported semiconductor manufacturing quality by enhancing imaging contrast and lithographic process control in advanced lithography nodes over the past decade. Through jointly optimizing the design of the illumination source and modifying the reticle patterns on the mask, the SMO techniques have provided a viable method to find the best lithography process for a given design rule. In SMO, process parameters such as the Exposure Latitude (EL), the Depth of Focus (DoF), the Mask Error Factor (MEF) can be improved through the definition of a cost function. In this presentation, we provide an example with a minimum pitch of 40 nm, which is commonly used for the 2~3 nm Back-End-Of-the-Line (BEOL) logic technology nodes. In this example, we will discuss the challenges and potential of our SMO technique and will offer recommendations for EUV SMO compensations for aberration. Our analysis indicates that SMO can continue to improve optimal pattern transfer capabilities by simultaneously optimizing both illumination source and mask design.

articleTitle: In-Device SEM-Based Overlay Metrology on VIA Layer of Logic Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Device shrinkage requires continuous tightening of the overlay (OVL) control. Systematic deviation between optical after-develop inspection (ADI) and after-etch inspection (AEI) OVL, known as non-zero offset (NZO), is critically important when applied to the scanner process. In the 28 nm logic process, the VIA layer relies on accurate OVL control to ensure device yield. In this paper, we discuss in-device SEM-based OVL metrology of the VIA layer to demonstrate the NZO gap and enable a better corrective methodology to minimize NZO in the advanced process control (APC) loop. In addition, the SEM OVL is valuable for providing more detailed and comprehensive OVL distributions, enabling high-order correction of the scanner process.

articleTitle: Read FF Performance Improvement by the Process Optimization in 4Xnm ETOX Nor Flash Non Self-Aligned FG Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: As the cell feature size shrink of ETOX Nor flash, the non self-aligned FG technique is investigated on account of its improvement in STI/FG poly gap-filling window and effective avoiding the residue caused by FG poly CMP. While, the non self-aligned process has brought about serious bin9 (read FF) failure issue. In this thesis, the failure field and mechanism were located and determined by EFA and PFA technologies. The poor performance of bin9 can be attributed to the cell active area damage due to the surface defects arising during the FG implantation annealing process. The cell read FF performance can be seen significant boost benefitting from the optimized process, in which oxygen is fed through the FG implantation annealing process.

articleTitle: Study on the removal rate and electrochemical corrosion of titanium in chemical mechanical polishing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Titanium (Ti), known for its high mechanical strength and excellent corrosion resistance, is commonly used in high-precision devices such as MEMS and integrated circuits. Consequently, the chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) of the titanium barrier layer plays a crucial role in the fabrication procedure. Nevertheless, owing to the distinctive physical and chemical characteristics of titanium, attaining a high removal rate for this material poses a significant challenge. The effect of Diethylenetriamine penta methylene phosphonic acid (DTPMP) as a complexing agent on the chemical mechanical polishing of titanium barrier layer was studied in this paper. The removal mechanisms of titanium were examined through polishing experiments and the corrosion current of titanium increases in the electrochemical experiments. When the concentration of DTPMP is 15mM, the removal rate of Ti is 960Å/min.

articleTitle: Test of higher-power Semiconductors: Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The rapidly evolving landscape of technology demands higher-power semiconductors [1] thereby posing significant challenges for engineers. Recent advancements in automotive, consumer electronics, IoT, PMICs, and LED drivers have heightened the need for increased operating voltage and current. However, testing these components for optimal yield and quality while managing costs has become increasingly complex. As a solution to these test challenges, this work presents a highly integrated ±50V, ±1A Parametric Measurement Unit (PMU) System-on-chip (SOC). PMU features of Four-Quadrant operation, accuracy, wide dynamic range and low-leakage enable the Device-under-test (DUT) to be tested in any operating condition. Moreover, the Automated Test Equipment (ATE) and DUT are protected by current- and voltage-clamps, and temperature, voltage, current and force/sense Kelvin faults alarms.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Synthetic Process of Bis(Diethylamino)Silane Based on Response Surface Methodology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, the synthesis process of bis(diethylamino)silane (BDEAS) was optimized by response surface methodology to improve its application in self-aligned double patterning (SADP) technology. In the study, dichlorodihydrosilane (DCS) and diethylamine (DEA) were used as the raw materials. The fitted regression equations of the factors on the yield of BDEAS were established by the central component rotational design (CCRD) method in the Design-Expert 12 software, and an analysis of variance was carried out to determine the significant influencing factors. The optimal conditions obtained from the optimization were a molar ratio of DEA to DCS of 8.894, a reaction temperature of 4.666 °C, and a reaction time of 18.279 min, resulting in BDEAS reaction yield reached 74.619%.

articleTitle: Study of Poly-Si Etch Rate Sensitivity with Pulsing mode of RF Powers for Soft-Landing Step in Gate Patterning Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Pulsed plasma has been developed to enlarge the etch control window for 32nm node technology and below. This article systematically studied the characteristics of etch rate sensitivity by orthogonal design of experiment (DOE) with this pulsed plasma. In addition, three types of pulsing modes in Cl2 and HBr based plasma are investigated to provide guidelines for the soft landing step in selective poly gate etching process.

articleTitle: A Snapshot Review on Salicide Technology Evolution for CMOS Fabrication from the Perspective of Process Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Salicide (self-aligned silicide) technology has been widely used in CMOS (complementary metal-oxide semiconductor) fabrication for several generations, to provide stable Ohmic contacts with low contact resistivity on active regions (source, drain and gate) and reduce sheet resistivity. As the CMOS device scaling continues, the salicide technology has evolved over the decades. This paper provides a concise overview of the development of salicide technology in CMOS fabrication, and summarizes the challenges and future prospects from a process integration perspective.

articleTitle: Predicting Film Thickness and Properties in CESL Process Based on CGAN
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Contact etch stop layer (CESL) process plays a pivotal role in semiconductor manufacturing, where accurate predicting the THK and RI of silicon nitride film in CESL process is crucial. This paper introduces a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN)-based prediction model, which simultaneously predicts film thickness and refractive index by CESL process recipes. By incorporating adversarial training, the model achieves superior accuracy compared to traditional methods such as Support Vector Regression (SVR) and XGBoost. This advancement allows for improved process optimization, reduced dependence on physical experiments, and better production quality control.

articleTitle: The Optimization of Metasurface lenses Fabrication based on Silicon Pillars within the fab's 12-inch production line
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Silicon photonic devices boast high transmission speeds and minimal loss, presenting vast potential for application in cutting-edge technological domains such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and quantum computing. Furthermore, silicon photonic devices can be integrated with CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) technology, leveraging its low power consumption and high integration density. The research endeavors on silicon photonic devices are undergoing a transition from the laboratory-scale stage to fab-scale production. This research is dedicated to the development of silicon photonic devices based on silicon pillars for metasurface lenses within 12-inch semiconductor manufacturing lines. It is observed that silicon pillars fabricated at 580 °C exhibit extensive porosity and cracking. Simultaneously, it was observed that the silicon film grown via LPCVD (Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition) at 580 °C exhibited remarkably large grain sizes and notably poor roughness. By altering the deposition temperature from 580 °C to 550 °C, a significantly compact silicon thin film was achieved, characterized by almost no crystallization. According to the refractive index of the newly developed Si film and fundamental mechanisms of the metalens, the film thickness and etching process were meticulously fine-tuned. Silicon pillars crafted from this refined adjustment demonstrated an impeccable quality, free of any cracks or voids. This study offers valuable insights and guidance for the industrial-scale fabrication of silicon pillars, thereby paving the way for the efficient mass production of silicon photonic devices.

articleTitle: Source Optimization Based on the Partially Coherent Imaging Model
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography (EUVL) has been utilized in the manufacturing of integrated circuit with 5nm node and beyond. Free Electron Laser (FEL) has the potential to substitute traditional Laser Produced Plasma (LPP) source in the EUV scanners for its high power ability. However, FEL has the characteristic of high spatial coherence, which would affect the results of computational lithography. This paper proposes source optimization (SO) method for EUVL, which takes into account the coherence of the light source. After considering the coherence among the source points in the "effective source", the partially coherent imaging model is firstly established. Then, an efficient SO method is discussed based on the gradient-based algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness of SO method is demonstrated from the simulation. Results illustrate that the proposed SO can reduce the lithographic pattern errors caused by the spatial coherence.

articleTitle: Study on the enhancement of surface quality of polyimide films by chemical mechanical polishing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The traditional chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) process has challenges in achieving high precision surface polishing of polyimide films. In this paper, the influence of different polishing pressure and polishing time on polishing speed and surface quality is studied. This research shows that the higher the polishing pressure, the faster the removal rate of polyimide film. Polishing time does not affect the removal rate. The choice of polishing pad has more influence on polishing rate and indicated roughness.

articleTitle: Ebara Tungsten CMP Process Defect Improvement
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical-mechanical planarization (CMP) is mainly used in the manufacture of very large scale integrated circuits (ICs), where global and local planarization of wafers is obtained through chemical and mechanical processes [1]. The CMP process requires a variety of consumables such as chemical, pad, disk, slurry, etc. Slurry is composed of an abrasive and various additives that improve the properties of the CMP process. Tungsten chemical-mechanical planarization (W CMP) has a special mechanism. Due to the high hardness of W, the choice of the hardness of the pad and the particles in the slurry is no longer a priority for the improvement of small scratches, but should focus on the uniformity of the W film and the surface properties of W film after CMP. Therefore, particles such as by-products and slurry residue after planarization should be removed from the surface. However, because nanoparticles have a strong electrostatic attraction to wafers [2], it is difficult to completely remove nanoparticles despite the cleaning process, and contamination remains on the wafer surface. Therefore, this paper mainly studies the improvement methods of polishing and cleaning process to reduce the retention rate of nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Effect of H2O2 on Poly Silicon Chemical Mechanical Planarization Particle Defect
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
