abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) has been extensively applied for semiconductor manufacturing to achieve planarity. As the feature size of devices shrinks, there are more stringent demands for CMP processes. In manufacture, forming floating gate or control gate by poly silicon CMP is one of the most important processes. Wherein, defect is one of the key factors for poly silicon CMP processed. Wettability is closely related to defect performance. H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> acts as oxidizer can increase wettability of poly-Si. In addition, excellent wettability is benefit to remove the particles from wafer surface, and good defect performance can be obtained.

articleTitle: Effect of Surfactants on the Properties of C-, A- and M-Plane Sapphire CMP
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) can attain nanoscale planarization of wafers through the coordinated combination of chemical erosion and mechanical detrition. The components of slurry directly determine the surface quality after polishing. In this study, the effects of cationic surfactants (CTAB) and anionic surfactants (SDS) on the surface roughness (Sq) and material removal rate (MRR) of A-, C- and M-plane sapphire were investigated. According to the data, both surfactants can improve the surface quality and MRR of sapphire, with SDS being superior to CTAB. The A-, C- and M-plane MRRs are 2.38 μm/h, 4.22 μm/h and 3.77 μm/h, respectively, when 0.02 wt% SDS is added, the corresponding Sq values are 0.213 nm, 0.234 nm and 0.202 nm, achieving optimal results.

articleTitle: A Wafer Temperature Control System for Advanced Technology Node Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Precise temperature control plays a crucial role of whole wafer uniformity in the manufacturing processes of advanced technology node. This paper presents AMEC’s wafer- temperature-control system, Durga II, which features adjustable local temperature fine tuning capabilities enabled by a separately controllable multi-zones electrostatic-chuck (ESC). The system demonstrates significant performance enhancements, achieving over 60% improvement in temperature distribution 3-sigma and range value on 300-mm wafer compared to traditional ESC. Additionally, Durga II enables post-etch amorphous-silicon thickness uniformity (TKU) of <10Å (3sigma) when plasma is involved, outperforming traditional CMP process and gas cluster ion beam (GCIB) methods as reported in prior studies. Beyond TKU, the system also supports critical dimension uniformity (CDU) tuning. Unlike traditional "feed-back" uniformity improvement relies on post etch performance, Durga II introduces a "feed-forward" tuning capability based on incoming film stack and CD/lithograph data. This system can be applied to both logic and memory chips etch manufacturing, which will greatly improve the accuracy and reliability in mass production by precise temperature control.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Safe Operation Area in Step-Gate NLDMOS
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The Safe Operating Area (SOA) of LDMOS devices is a critical parameter that defines the reliability and performance of power electronics systems. This paper presents the optimization strategy aimed at enhancing the SOA of the step gate NLDMOS devices by optimizing doping profiles and the field plates structure. The TCAD simulation results are presented to demonstrate that the modifications extend the SOA, enabling LDMOS devices to operate under higher voltage and current conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Reliability of Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS Technology Through Delicately STI Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS technology encounters significant reliability challenges at advanced technique node, particularly under high gate and drain voltages. This study is dedicated to the optimization of the shallow trench isolation (STI) structure. By extending the thermal oxidation duration of the liner SiO2, achieving a marked improvement in the interface smoothness between the STI and silicon, thereby reducing electric field concentration. This approach effectively alleviates interface degradation and lowers parasitic resistance. Furthermore, the incorporation of SiN and SiON interlayers in STI helps suppress the hot carrier injection (HCI) at the drain, mitigating device degradation. Optimizing STI edge quality and structural design substantially improves the overall performance of BCD devices.

articleTitle: SiC Trench Etch with Varying Aspect Ratio and Rounded Corner
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: SiC trench etching is one of the most challenging processes in the fabrication of wide-bandgap semiconductor power chips. Etch uniformity can be significantly improved (<2%) by adjusting the Power Source Ratio (PSR) and Gas Source Ratio (GSR). Optimizing the power and ratio of dual-frequency RF power supplies can achieve an etch rate of nearly 1 μm/min for SiC. Through the selection of power and gases, the effective etch selectivity (SiC/OX) can exceed 7, potentially reaching much higher values. The combination of Main Etching (ME) and Over-Etching (OE) can be employed to correct both bottom roundness and sidewall roughness. Furthermore, by refining the sidewall roughness of the initial photoresist through modification and subsequently treating the sidewalls of the oxide hard mask layer post-etching, the sidewall roughness of the oxide trench can be significantly mitigated. This refinement, in turn, minimizes the impact on the sidewall roughness of the SiC trench during the patterning process.

articleTitle: Automatic Defect Fatality Analysis and Killer-Defect Identification System Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence technology, more and more research has begun to explore the application of AI to the field of chip manufacturing. However,in the stage of mass production of chips, the problems existing in the current chip manufacturing process such as low efficiency of defect analysis and reliance on manual experience judgment have not been fully solved. To tackle this challenge, this paper introduces an intelligent defect analysis method that leverages the strengths of convolutional neural networks (specifically ResNet34) and Transformer architectures, creating a deep learning framework designed to automatically assess the effect of wafer surface defects on chip yield. Although traditional convolutional neural networks perform well in processing local pixel relationships, they often lack attention to the global background of images. The Transformer network introduces a global attention mechanism that pays more attention to the overall information and context of the image. By combining these two network structures, this paper designs a network framework that can capture both deep semantic information and global and contextual information. In order to increase the data set and improve the model’s capacity for generalisation, the group in the experiment used data enhancement technology after gathering a sizable amount of wafer surface defect image data. By comparing the experimental results, the proposed deep learning framework performs better than other advanced algorithms in the task of defect mortality analysis, especially in the analysis of wafer surface defect images, showing higher accuracy and efficiency. In addition, because of the use of a lightweight network, the structure can effectively meet the needs of large-scale production, and has strong promotion and application ability, as well as new ideas and methods for the intelligent development of related fields, so as to make the development of intelligent development in related fields more reasonable.

articleTitle: Etching Process Optimization of Deep Silicon Trench Sidewall Damage with High Aspect Ratio
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Deep trench etching process, as an important technology in the field of integrated circuit manufacturing, has been widely used in railway, new energy automobiles and smart grid in recent years. With the improvement of integration and device performance requirements, deep trench is developing towards higher aspect ratio and smaller CD, so that the deep trench etching process is facing severe challenges. As the aspect ratio increases, long-term exposure of the trench sidewall and hard mask to plasma results in sidewall damage and hard mask roughness which affect the device performance and production yield. In this paper, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>/He is used as the plasma source based on the single step process (SSP) etching process, focusing on the sidewall damage and hard mask roughness in the deep trench etching process, the mechanism and improvement methods were studied by optimizing the parameters such as bias voltage, chamber pressure and gas flow. In addition, a new etching method was proposed, which effectively solved the problems of sidewall damage and hard mask roughness.

articleTitle: An Analytics Methodology for Anomaly Detection In Machine Log Data
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Throughout the production of wafer in semiconductor manufacturing, a large number of log files are created. The information in logs generated by devices and applications can be used to assess the system’s health. The analysis of logs is crucial to verify whether equipment went smoothly. Manual review is insufficiently trustworthy, and takes much time and effort. In this paper, we present an algorithm for anomaly detection and raise alarms for potential incidents on time. In actual manufacturing, there are various abnormal conditions, including single point mutation, long-term trend change, anomalous divergence and abrupt change in numeric level, which are short of manual labeling. As a result, we innovatively modify and ensemble multiple segmentation algorithms, such as Mann-Kendall (M-K), Bernaola Galvan (BG) and Pettitt mutation test, and applied unsupervised learning i.e. Spectral Residual (SR) to better improve the performance. The results achieved by our approach are superior to other conventional time series anomaly detection methods.

articleTitle: Investigation of Performance Optimization in Bottom-Gate A-IGZO Thin-Film Transistors with Varying Thicknesses of PECVD-SiO2 Gate Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, bottom-gate a-IGZO TFTs with different thicknesses of PECVD-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate dielectric and W/L ratios were fabricated. The device with a thicker gate dielectric exhibits the better performance with a V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> of 72mV, a minimum SS of 155mV/dec, an I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON/OFF</inf> ratio of 3.72×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>, and an ultra-low leakage current of 1.23×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-14</sup>A/μm since its superior interface quality. This unique effect may be attributed to the diffusion of residual hydrogen into the IGZO channel, which passivates interface defects and provides more free carriers in the thicker gate dielectric.

articleTitle: Ultra-High Steep Ion Beam Etching by Employing Highly Dynamic Holder
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: For high-quality etching of incredibly small dimensions and complicated structures, it is essential to provide great control over sidewall morphology during the IBE process. This study presents a two-dimensional high precision adjustable motion sample holder and corresponded dynamic etching process for ion beam etching system designed to improve control over sidewall morphology and improve etching uniformity during the etching process. Structural enhancements increase the control accuracy to 0.1°, highly improving incident angle precision. It minimizes surface roughness in nanopatterning and ensures high-quality etching, meeting the strict requirements of sidewall contour control, improving the sidewall angle from 67.8° to 84.7°. The proposed solution significantly enhances etching uniformity for small, complex structures.

articleTitle: Exploration of Boundary Conditions for Capacitor Etching Methods Under the Background of Characteristic Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In analog IC circuits, capacitors are important passive components and mainly have functions such as bypassing, decoupling, filtering, and energy storage. Based on the 12-inch wafer manufacturing platform, this paper conducts parallel technical research aiming at the difficulties that appear in the etching process of capacitor devices, and explores the boundary conditions of capacitor etching methods. Through controlled experiments and combining characterization methods such as microscopic morphology analysis, element detection, and electrical performance detection, this research shows that innovative etching methods can improve process precision, expand the process window, and enhance the reliability of capacitor devices. The feasibility of using mild etching modification to form spacer morphology to protect the weak positions of Al MIM was studied; the good removal effect of the two-step flushing method on Al MIM polymer was analyzed; it was verified that the gas combination of Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> can better protect the dielectric layer and expand the process window; and by using Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/BCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/AR combined with a specific radio frequency power, stable etching of ultra-thin high-k dielectric was achieved, and the capacitance density can reach 595 fF/μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Investigation of Selector Characteristics for Scalable 1S1R Array
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the relationship between selector characteristics and the scalability of one-Selector-one-RRAM (1S1R) arrays. A 1S1R behavioral model is constructed using Verilog-A and the impact of selector characteristics on the performance of the 1S1R device is evaluated based on the characteristics of the 40 nm RRAM device. Furthermore, requirements for selectors in large-scale arrays are discussed based on the aforementioned models, revealing that an I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> down to hundreds of nA is demanded to realize a 1Mb 1S1R array.

articleTitle: The Investigation on Partial Via ETCH of Low-K in MHM AIO Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Considering better performance of low-k damage, Metal Hard-Mask (MHM) All-In-One (AIO) process is proposed and widely used from sub-65nm CMOS technology node. Via performance post partial via (PV) etch plays a significant role in final yield and reliability test. In this work, via etch performance is investigated from four points of via bottom roughness, via profile and pattern ER, via depth loading and TiN selectivity. Meanwhile, the effects of typical gases used in partial via etch and how they affect those key indexes are analyzed. Both etch mechanism and effective tuning knobs in via etching of low-k are provided in this study. Moreover, CH3F/N2 base shows the best overall performance in our study, deserving to be further investigated for development of advanced technology node.

articleTitle: Dual-Gate 2T0C Gain Cell for Multi-Bit Input Vector-Matrix Multiplication in-Memory Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, one novel dual-gate 2T0C is proposed for multi-bit input vector-matrix multiplication (VMM) in in-memory computing (IMC). Unlike the existing pulse-width modulation (PWM) method for implementing multi-bit input, the proposed approach utilizes pure voltage control to adjust the gate voltage of the dual-gate 2T0C, thus enabling high-speed computing. Validity of this multi-bit input scheme is confirmed by simulation with high linearity (~99.4%) of current versus gate bias of read transistor. In addition, the dual-gate 2T0C can achieve a high linearity (~97.9%) of current dependence on weight by using current programming. It indicates that the dual-gate 2T0C is promising for IMC.

articleTitle: Impact of X-ray Irradiation on Transfer Characteristics of Fin-FeFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study investigates the write and erase characteristics of ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) under different voltage conditions, as well as their electrical performance changes in irradiated environments. Through ±4V DC scanning and ±4V, 100 ns pulse operations, we observed a significant clockwise hysteresis in the device's transfer characteristics, with threshold voltage shifts representing the memory window of the FeFET. In the X-ray total ionizing dose irradiation tests, we analyzed the impact of irradiation on the electrical characteristics and storage properties of HZO-based FeFETs, revealing phenomena such as leftward drift of the transfer characteristic curves and reduction of the memory window. By integrating the radiation damage mechanisms of HZO films, we examined the influence of fixed trap charge generation on polarization strength and threshold voltage. The results indicate a significant degradation of electric field distribution and polarization characteristics in the HZO film after irradiation, affecting the device's memory capacity.

articleTitle: An Accuracy Scalable n-LDMOS Model for Drift Region
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The scalable of breakdown voltage in LDMOS is usually achieved by optimizing the length of the drift region through layout structure without adding additional process steps. By adding the relationship between the device performances (IV and CV) and the drift region parameters in the sub-circuit model, a novel LDMOS model was introduced to achieve voltage scalability for both IV and CV prediction. This model has been validated with a 60V to 100V scalable LDMOS in 0.18μm process platform.

articleTitle: Enhanced on-State Current and Reduced Contact Resistance in TiO2 Channel HfLaO FeFETs Via Post-Metallization Annealing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This work investigates the impact of post-metallization annealing (PMA) and post-deposition annealing (PDA) on the electrical properties of La-doped HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> FeFETs with a TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> channel. Compared to PDA, PMA enhances the on-state current by improving contact between the source/ drain electrodes and the channel, as well as increasing channel mobility. This work provides insights into the process impact on the performances of FeFETs with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> channels.

articleTitle: GIDL analysis of Novel 4F2 VCT architecture using TCAD simulations
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Vertical Channel Transistor (VCT) with 4F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> cell architecture has garnered significant attentions owing to its relaxed channel dimensions, good gate control and potential for future 3D integration. Moreover, VCT with secondary epitaxial channel (eVCT) features controllable channel thicknesses and self-aligned gate dimensions, facilitating improved manufacturability. However, Gate-Induced Drain Leakage (GIDL) has become a critical factor in degrading the performance of eVCT. In this work, we investigate the GIDL effect in eVCT structure by TCAD simulations. We observe that as the channel thickness decreases, Band-to-Band Tunneling (BTBT) is significantly enhanced, resulting in a more pronounced leakage current. Furthermore, variations in channel length and doping concentration play significant role in the leakage characteristics of the transistors. Our findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing these parameters to effectively mitigate GIDL and improve the performance of eVCT, particularly in advanced memory applications.

articleTitle: 3-D Mirror-Bit SONOS Memory Device with a Vertical-Channel Select Gate Transistor
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: To eliminate short channel effects of silicon-oxide-nitride-oxide-silicon (SONOS) memory, conventional 3-D SONOS flash arises but is too complicated to integrate with planar fabrication process. Herein, a simple 3-D mirror-bit SONOS memory device is proposed with well compatibility. This 3-D mirror-bit SONOS cell contains a vertical-channel select gate and two symmetrical planar memory gates. The operation on 3-D mirror-bit cells about erase, program and read was also designed to the avoid read disturb caused by hot carrier injection. Meanwhile, the electrical performances proves the effective operation on selected SONOS cell. This 3-D mirror-bit SONOS cell will inspired researchers to design more high-performance SONOS memory with small size, especially by simple planar fabrication process.

articleTitle: Research on PS-Level Clock Skew Testing Solution for High-Performance Clock Conditioner on V93000
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Clock regulators are commonly built into the systems that drive multiple high-speed AD/DA converters based on the JESD204B protocol. In these systems, precise synchronization among the clock outputs of the clock regulators is significant. The time deviation (skew) between channels is a key indicator for synchronization performance. It is usually at the picosecond (ps) level and is related to the accuracy of data transmission in the system. Generally, this parameter needs to be tested in mass production. Aiming at the challenges of high requirements for the number of test channels, high test stability, and high test costs of such parameters in mass production tests.This paper proposes a jitter histogram test method based on the PS5000 digital card of the V93000 platform. By dynamically adjusting the sampling edges, statistically analyzing the level-transition distribution over multiple cycles, and combining with a moving-average algorithm to extract the median value of the transition edges, high-precision measurement of multi-channel clock skew is achieved. Experiments show that this method has a consistent trend with the test results of an oscilloscope under different skew settings. The result fluctuation is controlled within ±6ps, and the PS5000 has abundant digital channel resources, which can realize the simultaneous testing of multiple devices and significantly reduce the mass-production cost.

articleTitle: Abnormal EPI Pattern Failure Mode Analysis with Virtual Farbication
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, we use process models to explore different potential causes of abnormal epitaxy growth patterning, including variations in RCD (recess critical dimension) depth, EPI growth-blocking surface impurities and combinations of different growth rates in multiple directions. These abnormal epitaxial growth patterns can degrade transistor performance and cause device failures.We observed that a deeper RCD creates a shallower flat area on the patterned surface and can cause concave epitaxial patterns. After EPI cleaning, if there are surface impurities that block normal EPI growth, the resulting growth can produce a skewed pattern similar to simulating a defect placed on the <100> and <110> surface planes.Finally, we considered whether differences in growth rates at different crystal surfaces can arise due to the subsequent SC1 wet cleaning process and NH4OH evaporate left by weak air flow in the production tool. Our failure mode simulation of this effect was consistent with the conditions encountered on an actual production line. Using our failure mode simulation methodology, we developed a failure mode hypothesis using simulation and quickly resolved a production line problem based upon these simulation results.

articleTitle: Modeling the Charging Effect on the Twisting Defects During High Aspect Ratio Etching of Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In high-aspect-ratio (HAR) plasma etching of dielectrics, random twisting is frequently observed. The charging effect is considered a potential factor influencing this twisting. We develop a novel model that takes into account the charging effect to simulate the profile evolution of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers and potential distribution during nanoscale HAR etching. The model also explores the effect of charging effect on twisting defects.

articleTitle: Optimization Directions and Solutions for AMHS in Large-Scale Semiconductor Fabs
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the growing global demand for advanced semiconductor chips, particularly in high-performance computing, 5G, automotive electronics, and IoT, GIGA fabs (ultra-large semiconductor fabrication plants) have emerged as a significant trend in the industry. These fabs leverage their immense production capacity, economies of scale, and advanced technologies. A key feature of GIGA fabs is their high level of automation, large-scale production, and complex technical requirements, which heavily rely on Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS). The AMHS in GIGA fabs is not only critical to production efficiency but also plays a vital role in yield control, turnover efficiency, and is foundational to achieving intelligent manufacturing and Industry 4.0. Therefore, optimizing and innovating AMHS for GIGA fabs is a crucial direction for the semiconductor industry's future development. Historically, AMHS solutions in GIGA fabs were monopolized by DFK/MURATEC, but with the rise of domestic AMHS integrators, new innovations are emerging in the actual implementation of FAB projects. This paper presents the innovative designs proposed by HIMC in response to the challenges faced by AMHS systems in GIGA fabs. Key innovations include the AI-driven crane control and dispatching system, software-defined track and transportation control systems, and practical applications of digital twins.

articleTitle: A Wafer-Level CMP Multi-Physics Modeling for IC Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) is a critical process in the manufacturing of modern integrated circuits, essential for achieving surface planarization and addressing the challenges posed by the reduction in device size. The CMP process is a complex, multi-disciplinary endeavor that involves mechanics, fluid dynamics, and chemistry, with numerous interrelated factors [1]. Given that research on CMP material removal mechanisms has lagged behind industrial practice, this paper presents a multi-physics field model, developed from the perspectives of contact mechanics and kinematics at the wafer scale. This model can predict wafer pressure distribution, material removal depth, and cumulative removal depth distribution under various process parameters. These predictions hold certain reference value and offer valuable guidance for the actual CMP process in integrated circuit manufacturing.

articleTitle: Automatically Monitor and Process V93K Pattern for Large Scale High-speed Digital Devices on ADVANTEST ATE platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: High speed digital device becomes popular due to the requirements for data transmission speed and efficiency in computing and artificial intelligence fields. Inside testing, high speed SCAN <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> and BIST, etc. occupy a large proportion in whole test program through protocol like JTAG, SPI <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup> etc.During pattern verification typical handling method is really timing consuming. A common and universal configured pattern solution is necessary. Based on these requirements, this paper introduces the relevant analysis, framework design and result implemented on ADVANTEST V93K ATE platform.

articleTitle: The Design of a Sub-Nanoampere (NA) Level Low-Offset Rail-To-Rail Unity-Gain Op-Amp
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The widespread use of consumer electronic devices presents a significant challenge in op-amp design, requiring ultra-low power consumption alongside broad dynamic response.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> Specifically, the design of a sub-nanoampere (nA) level low-offset rail-to-rail input/output op-amp is crucial. We have developed a robust nA level low-offset rail-to-rail unity-gain op-amp using TSMC CMOS process. The core circuit comprises a constant transconductance input stage, folded cascode gain stage, and Class-AB output stage. Additionally, to meet slew rate and offset requirements, we integrated a custom-designed transient current boosting module and chopping techniques.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Sensorless Condition Monitoring System for GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, a FPGA-based sensorless condition monitoring system for GaN HEMT was demonstrated. Constructing a resistive load switching circuit with a clamp circuit and a SiC MOSFET to isolate the gate and drain, the proposed field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based sensorless condition monitoring system improved the measurement accuracy. The system was used to investigate the impact of drain voltage and temperature on Ron. The increasing drain voltage led to an increased Ron can be explained by the "lucky electron" model. As the temperature increased, the atomic vibrations in the semiconductor lattice intensified, which influenced electron scattering and caused the GaN HEMT’s Ron rising.

articleTitle: Research on Methods to Improve the Server Usage Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the OPC process, engineers use the core of the server to run the script to correct the mask. If the number of the core is set inappropriately, it will greatly increase the normalized running time of the script, causing the core utilization efficiency to drop, resulting in serious waste of core resources. This paper analyzes the relationship between the core number setting in the script and the core utilization efficiency in detail, which can provide reference for the core number setting at each layer to improve server utilization efficiency and maximize the utilization of server resources, thus ensuring the timely publication of each layer.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Noise Measurements for Electromigration Characterization of Cu Interconnect Under Metal Barrier Punch Through Process Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the variation in electromigration (EM) reliability of Cu interconnect during punch through (PT) process optimization in BEOL. By using a relatively new test methodology based on low-frequency noise (LFN) measurements, the EM reliability of Cu wires with various bottom profiles under different optimization circumstances were discussed. The main advantages of LFN over the standard accelerated EM tests are that they are non-destructive, much faster, much cheaper, and closer to operation conditions. With the LFN technique, we find out that under metal barrier PT Process optimization, the metal lines with better cross section profiles tend to have better early EM characteristic.

articleTitle: Patterning Challenges and Perspectives Solutions in Advanced Dram Technology Nodes
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Bit cost ($/Gb) is key indicator for memory company and measurable by die density. To drive the die density up ultimately, industry solution is memory array technology tended to real 3D structure, that resulted in certain critical layer’s pattern definition changed from horizontal to vertical direction, and patterning process is from traditional lithograph and etch to more module process like deposition, lithography, dry etch and wet etch etc., In order to overcome the new patterning challenge, module process co-optimization is must. In this paper, we evaluate the correlation between line CD uniformity and thin film roughness in 3D structure, and finally find a tunable knob to improve the CDU about 25%.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Optimization Algorithm for the Automatic Design of Analog Integrated Circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, we have explored the use of hierarchical optimization technique to automatically design low dropout regulator. When we use genetic algorithm for multi-objective optimization, the increase of design variables will greatly increase the difficulty of optimization. Therefore, we divide the whole circuit into different levels and only upload the sub circuits’ combination of design parameters to reduce the design variables and shorten the optimization time. In our work, we have explored the optimization results under different constraints, and compared them with the direct optimization results systematically.

articleTitle: Extract Parameters from Cv Curves Using A Machine Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Parameter extraction from CV curves is crucial in the development and optimization of gate stack technology. Traditional ways of obtaining these parameters are time consuming and sometimes require additional measurements. In this paper, we extract the work function (WF), oxide thickness (Tox) and substrate doping concentration (Nsub) from CV curves using a regression-based machine learning method. A dataset containing 2500 curves each for Cgg, Cgb and Cgc is generated by CVC (NCSU) and Ngspice simulation, with 80% data used for training and 20% for testing. The training results show the extracted Tox and WF have maximum errors of ± 1% and ± 0.5%, respectively. Our trained model is further validated in the parameter extraction from silicon CV data, and expected to be used for fast and automated analysis.

articleTitle: Accelerating the Physical Design of Large FPGAS Through Divide-And-Conquer Methodology
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The scale and complexity of circuit designs deployed on FPGA has surged with the increasing capacity of FPGA devices. At the same time, the runtime of physical design has grown exponentially, significantly extending the cycle of design iteration for engineers. To address this issue, we propose an automated, split-and-parallel physical design flow to accelerate the deployment of large-scale circuits on FPGA. We partition the original design into multiple sub-designs, perform placement and routing of each sub-design parallelly, and then merge them together. Experimental results show that our flow achieves 1.85X-2.7X speedup compared to standard Vivado flow with trivial degradation on design performance.

articleTitle: Monitoring & Testing of Nanoparticle Contaminants
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: It will be described semiconductor and its supply chain for particle pollutant detection down to 3nm or 9nm, including several segments:1. What's the detection limit among OPC, CPC and Raman optics for the particle pollutant testing esp. in the semiconduction industry;2. What are the commercial particles and particle precursors equipment by using NCPC technology in the liquid or wet chemicals;3. What's the minimum detection size in this periodƒ And what are the liquid substance or chemicals testedƒ4. Meanwhile, what's the different among OPC, CPC and Raman or othersƒ5. To describe the comparison testing data to depict how to detect CMP slurry, hydrochloric acid and sulfuric acid.

articleTitle: Effective and Innovative ATPG solutions to shorten TTM based on V93000
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Due to the rapid development of consumer electronics, consumer fabless companies in sectors like Mobile Application Processor Baseband (APBB), Microcontroller Unit (MCU) often face the challenge of tight time-to-market (TTM) targets, while the development of Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) program is quite challenging for fresh engineer. In this paper, we have introduced Tpzilla solution, which is an effective and innovative automatic test program generator (ATPG) solution based on Advantest’s V93000 platform. This solution provides a friendly and modern GUI to develop test program with step-by-step wizard, making TP development much easier for V93000 beginner, greatly improved the offline program development efficiency and reduced learning cost.

articleTitle: Gapfill Improvement with Helium /Argon Sputter Gas of HDP FSG in Power Device
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Low dielectric constant (low-k) materials are crucial in advancing integrated circuit technology. Fluorosilicate glass (FSG), with a lower dielectric constant than pristine undoped SiO₂, is widely used as a dielectric material in the intermetal dielectric (IMD) layers of 180nm-130nm CMOS devices [1]. It reduces interconnect capacitance, mitigates RC delays, and enhances device performance. Traditional high-density plasma (HDP) FSG deposition processes utilize argon (Ar) as the primary sputtering gas, adjusting the deposition-to-sputtering (D/S) ratio for gapfill. However, Ar-Based one-step HDP deposition often struggles to achieve perfect gapfill, frequently resulting in voids or metal clipping. This study introduces helium (He) as the primary sputtering gas in a one-step FSG HDP process to enhance gapfill performance, achieving void-free and metal clipping-free results while significantly widening the D/S process window. Compared to conventional Ar-Based deposition, the helium-based process increased throughput on Lam Research Corp.’s SPEED® Max platform by 20% and improved sputtering rate uniformity from 4.7% to 1.0%.

articleTitle: Analysis and Improvement of High Temperature LU Problem in CMOS RF Chip
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, regarding the issue of high-temperature Latch-up (LU) on chips, we discovered a path for CMOS RF (Radio Frequency) chip to excite LU: under high temperature conditions the power supply passes through the clamp cell to the analog ground, the analog ground travels through the packaging path to the digital ground, and through the first level protection diode to the ESD discharge path of the digital IO pin. The ESD current causes the clamp to conduct, thereby triggering LU. Meanwhile, in order to improve the reliability of the chip, we have taken measures such as strengthening the power network and reducing resistance to avoid possible LU.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Patterning of Directed Self-Assembly (DSA) Lithography Via Universal Orientation Control Method
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Directed self-assembly (DSA), as an emerging nano-manufacturing technology, demonstrates significant potential in advanced nodes in semiconductor field. This paper reports a method for controlling the domain orientation of fluorinated block copolymers (named as FV-1) on graphoepitaxy template, successfully producing high-resolution line and contact hole patterns with dimensions as small as 8 nm, without using molecular brushes or topcoat materials. This method realizes the combination with traditional lithography techniques, overcoming the limitations of lithography when scaling down. And the process flow is relatively simple, highlighting its strong application prospects.

articleTitle: A 60GHz Four-Stage Cascaded LNA for 802.11ad Protocol with 22.3db Gain and 3.45 Noise Figure
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper introduces a 60GHz low noise amplifier (LNA) designed in a 65nm CMOS process, addressing the challenge of optimizing gain and noise figure (NF) simultaneously in millimeter wave LNAs. The amplifier uses L-type and π-type matching networks for input and output matching. The common-source LNA with source degeneration is analyzed. By eliminating the source degradation inductance in the four-stage LNA, overall gain and noise performance are improved. Post-simulation results demonstrate that the LNA can achieve a gain of 19.90~22.3dB and a NF of 3.45~3.66dB at 57~66GHz. The amplifier's performance is competitive with similar LNAs in terms of frequency and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Adhesion Properties of Sio2 Film by Gas Atmosphere Pre-Soak and Low Deposition Rate Initial Layer in PECVD Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) films, especially those deposited by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), are commonly used as dielectric layer layers in semiconductor devices and, at the same time, as effective bonding layers between other functional layers, such as silicon nitride, titanium nitride, and so on. When the interlayer stress is not balanced, or the condition of wafer bevel is complex after multi etching and scrubbing processes, the interface of films may flake off from each other due to insufficient adhesion. The formed large peeling defects might affect the subsequent processes and the capability of devices. Therefore, increasing the adhesion of the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer is important for the reduction of such defects. In this study, adding a gas atmosphere preheating step and an initial step with low deposition rate, can effectively enhance the adhesion of the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films in the PECVD process. Nano-scratch experiments show that the mechanical properties of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films deposited with the pretreatment step are significantly improved from those deposited without the pretreatment step. The change in properties depends on the preheating time and the deposition rate of the initial step. Experiments on structured wafers show that the number of peeling defects is significantly reduced for the pretreated samples in both the center and edge regions. It is hypothesized that the gas preheating step was effective in making the wafer surface more uniformly heated, which is of benefit to the formation the chemical bonding between reactive precursors and wafer surface, as well as, the consistency of the growth rate of initial island.

articleTitle: The Application of an Almost Forgotten Theory to Explain the Leakage Current Mechanism in State-Of-The-Art High-K Dram Mim Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In 1969, a theory was proposed that the leakage current-voltage (I-V) characteristics sometimes appear to follow the Poole-Frenkel theory for one polarity and the Schottky emission theory for the other polarity. Subsequently, this theory was almost forgotten. In this paper, the author will apply this almost forgotten theory to explain the leakage current mechanism in DRAM MIM capacitors.

articleTitle: Study of Breakdown Voltage Optimization in 1100V HVIC NLDMOS Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study presents an in-depth investigation of the breakdown voltage characteristics of a 1100V High-Voltage Integrated Circuit (HVIC) NLDMOS device utilizing comprehensive two-dimensional TCAD simulations. Our findings indicate that the surface electric field can be significantly reduced by implementing P-type implant in the drift region. It is essential to optimize the energy and dose of the P-type implant in relation to the substrate resistivity, alongside the thickness and resistivity of the N-type epitaxial layer. The insights derived from this research pave the way for improved device design strategies aimed at enhancing breakdown voltage performance.

articleTitle: A Continuous Data Sampling Solution for MEMS ASIC Test on V93000
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: With the development of MEMS sensors, the testing of internal ASIC as a signal processing module has become increasingly important and complex. The embedded FIFO is widely used in MEMS sensors as a buffer to store samples and can effectively reduce the frequent access between the system and MEMS. For typical ADC test, ATE can capture output data directly or access corresponding RAM which restores a piece of ADC sampling data. In this paper, ATE could only get sampling data from the FIFO which is connected to the output ADC. However, the data stream update rate in the FIFO is inconsistent due to the different data transfer rates of different ADCs. Therefore, it is difficult to match the ATE data acquisition rate with the FIFO updated data stream. In order to get a continuous piece of data with satisfactory length for further DSP and evaluation, the test program should be carefully designed to deal with the output data rate of the FIFO.Hence, this paper provides an efficient continuous sampling solution on the V93000. A four-layer COGO node procedure structure is designed. This solution can complete low-latency sampling inside the ATE to avoid data overflow and ensure the continuity of test data. There is no need to send the sampling data back to the host computer for judgment in the whole data sampling process, so the overall test time is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Passive BLE Wake-Up Receiver with Single Sideband(SSB) Backscatter System
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Low-Power Passive BLE Wake-up Receiver, which is integrated with a Single Sideband (SSB) Backscatter System. The proposed system achieves remarkable energy efficiency, consuming only 200 nW for On-Off Keying (OOK) and 2.8 μW for Bluetooth Low Energy Gaussian Frequency Shift Keying (BLE-GFSK). Notably, during BLE broadcast backscatter at 1.0 Mbps, the system achieves an energy consumption as low as 2 pJ/bit. The system is fabricated using a 55 nm CMOS process, occupying a total area of 0.46 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, including I/O pads, and fully satisfies the stringent power requirements of energy-harvesting IoT applications.

articleTitle: Study of UV Cure Effect on Peald Sinx WER in 3D Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: We investigated the effects of different ultraviolet (UV) cure time 1 min/5min/10min and output power 75%/85%/95% on PEALD SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> (with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) film thickness (THK) and dilute HF @30:1 wet etch rate (WER). With the increase of UV cure time, the transmission electron microscope (TEM) THK of PEALD SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> film showed little change for both NPW (non-pattern wafer) & PW (pattern wafer). Though WER also no obviously changes for the NPW, it shows trend down for nearly all locations in the 3D architecture. Especially for UV cure 10 min, the PEALD SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> film WER shows evident decrease, pocket lateral maximum optimizes ~70%, changes from 21.4 nm/min to 6.3 nm/min on average for 6 Tiers. Due to the limited transmission of UV wavelengths, the effect of UV cure on PEALD SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> film WER reduction weakens as depth increases. Also we found the UV lamp power has a positive effect on lowering the WER. Next we can merge the long UV cure time and large UV lamp power for the WER further reduction.

articleTitle: A Novel Load-Si-Cut SOI Nanosheets Transistors with Ultrathin SiGe Cladded Si Channel Structure to Suppress Leakage and Enhance Driven Current
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this article, we propose a novel load-Si-cut silicon-on-insulator (SOI) nanosheets transistors (NSFETs) with ultrathin SiGe cladded Si channel structure, named as LSC-SOI NSFETs, improving the drive current and suppressing leakage issues in the conventional SOI (C-SOI) NSFETs. The electrical characteristics of PMOS device, inverters and ring oscillators (RO) of C-SOI and LSC-SOI NSFETs were investigated using 3D technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Ambipolar Ferroelectric Tunnel FINFET Based Computing-in-Memory for Quantized Neural Networks with High Area- and Energy-Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, for the first time, a novel ambipolar ferroelectric tunnel FET (FeTFET) based computing-in-memory (CIM) scheme is proposed and experimentally demonstrated for quantized neural networks (QNNs) with high area- and energy-efficiency. By leveraging non-monotonic transfer characteristic of ambipolar tunnel FET (TFET) for signed multiplication and utilizing the nonvolatile ferroelectric gate modulation for weight storage, the signed CIM cell with weight precision expansion can be implemented by one single FeTFET device based on 14-nm technology node platform. Based on the proposed FeTFET-based CIM design, QNNs for typical pattern recognition tasks are demonstrated with high accuracy and energy efficiency, showing its significant potential for edge AI applications.

articleTitle: The Investigation and Detection of Poly Residue Defect for 28 HKMG Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the 28 high-k advanced semiconductor process, we always use new metals for example AL to replace the NMOS and PMOS poly silicon gate electrodes. It needs to metal deposition into the poly groove which requires metal filling coverage, but also required no residue and block. The poly residue is a key defect in the 28HK process, will cause the loss of the final chip yield and reliability issue. We found that the poly residue closely related to a key parameter of horn height. More interesting, Whether the horn is too high or too low will finally result in poly residue defect. so the root causes of poly residue was very intricately . In this study, we discussed every fail model of poly residue defect in depth, and provide effective improvement actions. Summary proposes effective improvement methods to improve factory yield.

articleTitle: Effect Of Sputtering Paraments On The Surface Morphology And Electrical Properties Of Thin Film Resistors
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In the field of integrated circuits, the electrical characteristics of resistors affect the performance of the whole circuit. Especially the temperature characteristics can cause instability in the output of the circuit. There have been many literatures to study the effect of different factors on the characteristics of resistors, but few literatures to study what influences these factors including the surface roughness of thin film resistors. In this paper, the effect of fabrication procedures on the surface topography of thin film is investigated. It is shown that changing fabrication procedures paraments can have a great influence on the thin film resistors (TFR). This research uncovers a novel pathway to strengthen the functionality of nanosized resistors.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Investigation about Channel Size Effects on PBTI and SILC in Planar High-K MG NFETs
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this paper, a full-scale debate is under way on the effects of channel length and width on PBTI of High-K metal gate(High-K MG) NMOS device. The transistors used in this research are manufactured on Huali-28nm High-K MG CMOS platform. The experimental results shown that the PBTI induced Vt degradation declined when decrease the width of device. Gate leakage also exhibited strong correlation with channel size whether in strong or weak electric field. The underlying mechanisms are investigated and the results revealed it is attributed to the modulation of process related pre-exciting defects in the High-K bulk. Otherwise, PBTI stress applied at transistors with different gate length exhibiting two distinctly different degradation trends. This anomalous phenomenon is primarily stems from the effective work function(EWF) diversity between long and short transistors, this results in the actual voltage drop across gate oxide(Vox) existing discrepancies so too does the vertical electric field.

articleTitle: The Challenges and Solutions of Damascus Copper Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: The continuous scaling down in the logic device has presented numerous engineering and manufacturing challenges in Cu interconnection. High resistivity, poor reliability and insufficient filling capacity are encountered. The main failure mode are narrower top opening and discontinuous Cu seed at the sidewall. These weak points are trade off and the process has reached its limit. Excavating the maximum efficiency of the additives, optimizing plating current curve during gap fill and cooperation between pre & post process as well as fast root cause finding are very important. Three failure cases are analyzed in this paper, where it well discloses that smaller gap fill current during ECP is good for excavate the maximum efficiency of the additives, while it is not friend to Cu seed protection. A suitable current is request base on the failure model. Reliability problem is strongly correlate to cumulative thermal and airborne molecular contamination, so both equipment and Foup environment control is essential. Entry process of Cu plating is key step, in which a novel visible method is designed to simulate the liquid touch line evolution, thereby, to help solve pits defect after fully understand micro bubble trapping in the trench.

articleTitle: Cd Step Application in Edge Air Layer Structure Measurement for Bulk Acoustic Resonator
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: A vital component of modern communication systems, bulk acoustic wave resonators (BAW) function as filters, oscillators, and sensors. In a BAW device, the acoustic waves are confined within a specific region to achieve efficient resonance. The air ring structure, including the edge air layer structure, prevents acoustic energy from leaking. However, measuring the critical dimensions (CD) of edge air layers is challenging. In this paper, we will show how Onto Innovation’s IVS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> 220 optical overlay and CD metrology system can measure the edge air layer structure using a CD step application. The IVS 220 system provides good repeatability and high throughput [130 wph, five (5) fields, one (1) site per field]. In addition, the IVS 220 system also can be used for overlay measurement, CD measurement (including angle CD and diameter of the circle or hole), and Z height measurement.

articleTitle: Design of Ferroelectric FET-based Symmetric Computing-in-Memory Array with Simultaneous Weight Gradient Calculation and Weight Update for on-Chip Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In this work, a novel ferroelectric FET (FeFET) based symmetric computing-in-memory (CIM) array enabling simultaneous weight gradient (ΔW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) calculation and weight update is proposed for on-chip learning with reduced latency. By utilizing stochastic computing (SC) scheme with novel bipolar pulse streams for ΔW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> calculation and utilizing the output pulses of SC for update of FeFET weights, the ΔW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> calculation and weight update of backpropagation (BP) learning are in-situ realized simultaneously for the whole array of CIM cell with special designed tri-state XNOR gate. Moreover, through the design of symmetric differential input and readout based on reference FeFET, four-quadrant vector-matrix multiplication (VMM) of configurable forward and backward propagation are implemented in the FeFET-based CIM array. Based on the design, image recognition’s neural network is demonstrated with a high accuracy of 95.33% and reduced hardware cost, showing great potential for on-chip learning.

articleTitle: Effect of Green Surfactant ADS on Properties of Copper CMP Slurry
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: In copper (Cu) film chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) of integrated circuits, the surfactant can disperse the abrasive and enhance the stability of the slurry to achieve a more consistent material removal rate (MRR) and low surface roughness. In this paper, the roles of anionic surfactant ammonium dodecyl sulfate (ADS) and fatty alcohol polyether (JFCE) on the MRR, surface roughness and slurry stability of copper were studied. Compared with the JFCE, the same concentration of anionic surfactant ADS can promote the dispersion of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> abrasive particles more rapidly and form a stable suspension.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enhanced Equivalent Circuit Modeling for Advanced Packaging Components
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Signal integrity analysis for advanced packaging is essential for guiding design and manufacturing processes and is crucial to optimizing chip performance. In this paper, we propose a general modeling method for advanced packaging components that employs MLPs to predict the parameters of equivalent circuits, thereby characterizing signal transmission over a wide frequency range. Compared to traditional empirical formulas, our approach offers higher accuracy and computational efficiency, providing valuable guidance for the design and manufacturing of advanced 3D integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Hafnium Missing Induced SRAM HTOL Fail in Scaled HKMG Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) test chip HTOL (High Temperature Operating Life) test was frequently used for new platform product qualification and bit cell qualification. The Vmin shift outliers occurred during HTOL stress induced Vmin fail spec in deep sub-micron High-K metal gate (HKMG) technology. All fail bits showed small particles across deformed gate and hafnium missing. These particles were deduced to exist before gate oxide formation, and could be significantly reduced by replacing dual-gate etch batch clean with single wafer cleaning process. Small particles should be carefully controlled at the beginning of platform development, especially in advanced tech nodes with high density SRAM that vulnerable to defects.

articleTitle: Simulation Optimization and Fabrication Verification Study of Ion Implantation In 12-Inch CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: This study utilizes TCAD to model and simulate the CMOS fabrication process, focusing on the impact of ion implantation parameters on critical electrical characteristics such as threshold voltage, saturation current, and breakdown voltage. Specifically, it explores the effects of dose, energy, and tilt during the Pocket Implant process. A comparative analysis of simulation result was conducted to obtain the optimal ion implantation recipe. The optimized recipe was then applied to actual fabrication, showing a high accuracy in predicting key electrical metrics. This approach provides valuable insights for optimizing 12-inch CMOS technology while reducing development time and costs.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Random-Access Memory at 77K
publicationTitle: 2025 Conference of Science and Technology of Integrated Circuits (CSTIC)
abstract: Magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) is a competitive candidate in several applications. To characterize its performance in low temperature environments, MRAM was immersed in liquid nitrogen and subjected to a series of tests. The results demonstrate that as the temperature decreases, the electrical properties such as tunnel magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) and coercive field become more ideal, which positions MRAM as a promising candidate for low-temperature applications.
